title: Hard-core Bosons In Action: Applications To Quantum Circuits
authors: Michael Epping David Emmanuel-Costa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of algebraic frameworks based on complex Clifford algebras for the representation and simulation of quantum circuits has been discussed in the literature. Recently, an alternative algebraic approach employing hard-core bosons has been proposed. Hard-core bosons provide a natural representation of multi-qubit systems, in which the tensor-product structure is realized directly and no sign corrections are required, in contrast to realizations based on complex Clifford algebras. Although both approaches are formally equivalent, the hard-core boson formulation exhibits computational advantages. This work reviews and extends the hard-core boson algebra for circuit simulation and presents an efficient implementation. A performance comparison with IBM Qiskit shows substantially improved execution times for simulations. Moreover, a new application is introduced in which the hard-core boson formalism is combined with genetic algorithms for quantum circuit synthesis.
tldr: The paper presents a hard-core boson algebraic framework for quantum circuit simulation and synthesis, with performance improvements over Qiskit.
motivation: Efficient simulation and synthesis of quantum circuits are important for quantum computing, and alternative algebraic approaches may offer computational advantages.
method: The authors review and extend the hard-core boson algebra for circuit simulation, implement it efficiently, and combine it with genetic algorithms for circuit synthesis.
result: The hard-core boson implementation shows substantially improved execution times compared to IBM Qiskit for simulation tasks.
conclusion: The hard-core boson formalism is a promising tool for quantum circuit simulation and synthesis, with potential for further applications.

title: Quantum Multi-Party Threshold Private Set Intersection With Explicit Cardinality Testing
authors: Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Fengxia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threshold private set intersection (TPSI) allows parties to reveal their intersection only when its cardinality reaches a prescribed threshold. Existing quantum TPSI protocols typically rely on a third party (TP) to interpret the final results, which deviates from the cardinality-testing paradigm of TPSI. In this paper, we propose a quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing. Our protocol develops a rotation-based quantum construction in which single-photon sequences are sequentially processed through participant-side data rotations, TP--participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors: TP can complete the final measurement, but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of the outcomes. Based on these hidden measurements, we further realize the threshold decision through an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only \(\mathbf 1[|\bigcap_i X_i|\ge \tau]\) before conditional intersection reconstruction. We prove the correctness and security of the proposed protocol, and further validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations implemented on the IBM platform.
tldr: A quantum multi-party threshold private set intersection protocol with explicit cardinality testing using rotation-based encoding and oblivious linear evaluation.
motivation: Existing quantum TPSI protocols rely on a third party to interpret results, deviating from the cardinality-testing paradigm; this work aims to provide explicit threshold testing without revealing semantic meaning.
method: The protocol uses single-photon sequences with participant-side data rotations, TP-participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations to produce hidden-label measurement vectors, then applies OLE-based inner product and garbled circuits for threshold decision.
result: The protocol is proven correct and secure, and its feasibility is validated via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM's platform.
conclusion: The proposed protocol achieves explicit cardinality testing in a multi-party setting without revealing the intersection size beyond the threshold, advancing quantum private set intersection.

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a complete mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump process theories.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and continuum limits that recover diffusion results.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that treats jump and diffusion processes on equal footing, enabling consistent analysis of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework offers a rigorous foundation for studying stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuations in systems with both continuous and discrete dynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.

tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: Defines new control parameters beyond stellar rank and uses them to design and optimize optical circuits for non-Gaussian state generation.
result: Achieves orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The proposed control parameters enable scalable and efficient generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity approaching that needed to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a highly sensitive technique, tracking the freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional entropy, achieving sensitivity that constrains the extraction of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path toward measuring topological entropy in fractional quantum Hall systems, but the current results are more about thermodynamic characterization than direct information-theoretic or thermodynamic principles.

tldr: The paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is essential for universal quantum computing, but existing methods often require non-planar geometries or high overhead.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that use lattice surgery and a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on a planar 2D color code.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and compatible with nearest-neighbor couplings, achieving fault tolerance with reduced overhead compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips using color codes.

result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantages for matrix function computations, guiding future algorithm design.

result: They show that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for small patches, reducing quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to combine quantum and classical resources for variational algorithms, though limited to small subregions.

conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where such violations occur, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, internal resonances, or hierarchical structures, and shows how to design materials that exploit these effects.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but stem from misapplied assumptions; this insight can guide the development of materials with superior properties.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and homology computation without relying on oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices and coherent interference, and they build unitary encodings for clique complexes.
result: They achieve apparent superpolynomial quantum speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA1-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant speedups for topological data analysis and related computational problems, with potential applications in complexity theory.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: Derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical interferometers that provide necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Quantum linear optics without post-selection cannot produce arbitrary quantum states, limiting applications that require entangled resources; a deeper understanding of state preparation constraints is needed.
method: Identifies conserved quantities (invariants) under the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians, and uses them to derive necessary conditions for state transformation and a lower bound on distance to target states.
result: The invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound on the distance between output and target states, enabling elimination of impossible evolutions.
conclusion: Future state preparation methods in linear optics must consider these invariants to avoid impossible transformations, aiding the search for useful entangled states like NOON states.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras for QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle and complete graphs.
motivation: Understanding the expressiveness and trainability of variational quantum algorithms is crucial for their practical use; barren plateaus hinder training, and DLA analysis offers a way to characterize them.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on DLA dimensions and centers for general graphs, and for cycle and complete graphs they construct explicit bases and decompose the DLA into center and semisimple components.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a 1-dimensional center and a semisimple part isomorphic to copies of sl(2), and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2-1 with an explicit basis.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA DLAs, confirming the absence of barren plateaus for specific graphs and offering tools for further study.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite purities) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial sample complexity for states with matrix product state structure.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical learning was unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from a polynomial number of samples, benchmarking on Haar random states and random MPS.
result: TCI can efficiently learn the entanglement feature for states that are themselves MPS or have low entanglement feature complexity; they identify eigenstates of 1D systems where this holds.
conclusion: The learned entanglement feature enables quantifying distances between entanglement patterns and finding optimal 1D orderings, suggesting practical utility for entanglement analysis.

title: Operator Delocalization In Disordered Spin Chains Via Exact Mpo Marginals
authors: Jonnathan Pineda-Jiménez, Mario Collura, Gianluca Passarelli, Procolo Lucignano, Davide Rossini And Angelo Russomanno
abstract: We investigate operator delocalization in disordered one-dimensional spin chains by introducing—besides the already known operator mass—a complementary measure of operator complexity: the operator length. Like the operator nonstabilizerness, both these quantities are defined from the expansion of time-evolved operators in the Pauli basis. They characterize, respectively, the number of sites on which an operator acts nontrivially and the spatial extent of its support. We show that both the operator mass and length can be computed efficiently and exactly within a matrix-product-state framework, providing direct access to their full probability distributions, without resorting to stochastic sampling. Applying this approach to the disordered spin-1/2 chain, we find sharply distinct behaviors in non-interacting and interacting regimes. In the Anderson-localized case, operator mass, length, and operator entanglement entropy rapidly saturate, signaling the absence of scrambling. By contrast, in the many-body localized (MBL) regime, for arbitrarily weak interactions, all quantities exhibit a robust logarithmic growth in time, consistent with the known logarithmic light cone of quantum-correlation propagation in MBL. We demonstrate that this behavior is quantitatively captured by an effective -bit model and persists across system sizes accessible via tensor-network simulations.
tldr: This paper studies operator delocalization in disordered spin chains using exact MPO marginals, revealing distinct behaviors in Anderson-localized and MBL regimes.
motivation: Understanding operator complexity and scrambling in disordered quantum systems is key to characterizing many-body localization and thermalization.
method: The authors introduce operator length as a measure of operator complexity and compute its full probability distribution exactly using matrix-product state (MPS) techniques.
result: In the MBL regime, operator mass, length, and entanglement entropy show robust logarithmic growth, consistent with an effective l-bit model, while in the Anderson-localized case they saturate.
conclusion: The exact MPO marginal approach provides a powerful tool to study operator delocalization and scrambling in disordered spin chains without stochastic sampling.

title: Quantum Typicality Survives non-Abelian Gauge Constraints: Exact Analytical Prediction Confirmed In $su(2)$ Lattice Gauge Theory
authors: Samuel L. Braunstein Zhi-Wei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arguments for emergent spacetime require that quantum typicality, the generic absence of inter-subsystem correlations, persists on the physical Hilbert space of a gauge theory, where non-Abelian constraints could in principle inject geometry-supporting entanglement. Using [MATH] lattice gauge theory on two-dimensional tori ([MATH] up to [MATH]), we show that it does: the typical mutual information between strictly disjoint links matches an exact parameter-free analytical prediction combining a microcanonical baseline with Haar-random fluctuations. The Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian generates correlations from states of definite geometry (such as the electric vacuum), while generic states show only regression to the mean, establishing that the arrow of correlation growth requires a non-generic initial condition.
tldr: Quantum typicality, the absence of inter-subsystem correlations, is shown to persist in non-Abelian lattice gauge theory, with mutual information matching an analytical prediction.
motivation: To understand whether gauge constraints in non-Abelian theories can generate entanglement that supports emergent spacetime, contrary to typicality.
method: Analytical calculation of mutual information in SU(2) lattice gauge theory on tori, compared with exact diagonalization for small lattices.
result: Typical mutual information between disjoint links follows a microcanonical baseline plus Haar-random fluctuations, with no significant entanglement from gauge constraints.
conclusion: Quantum typicality survives non-Abelian gauge constraints, and correlation growth requires non-generic initial conditions.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates whether quantum typicality—the generic absence of correlations between subsystems—holds in the physical Hilbert space of non-Abelian gauge theories, specifically SU(2) lattice gauge theory on two-dimensional tori. The authors argue that emergent spacetime scenarios rely on typicality to avoid geometry-supporting entanglement from gauge constraints. Using exact diagonalization for Hilbert space dimensions up to 4,193, they compute mutual information between strictly disjoint links (separated by at least one lattice spacing) for random states drawn from the physical Hilbert space. They find that the typical mutual information matches an analytical prediction combining a microcanonical baseline (the average over all states) with Haar-random fluctuations. The Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian generates correlations from states of definite geometry (e.g., the electric vacuum), but generic states show only regression to the mean, implying that correlation growth requires a non-generic initial condition. The results support the persistence of typicality in gauge theories, with implications for emergent spacetime and the arrow of time.
key_contributions: Demonstrates that quantum typicality persists in the physical Hilbert space of SU(2) lattice gauge theory, despite non-Abelian constraints.
Provides an exact parameter-free analytical prediction for typical mutual information between disjoint links, combining microcanonical average and Haar-random fluctuations.
Shows that the Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian generates correlations only from non-generic initial states (e.g., electric vacuum), while generic states exhibit regression to the mean.

title: Fault Tolerant Computation Of The Static Structure Factor And Finite Size Effects
authors: Rishabh Bhardwaj, Alexander Reed Mu\~noz, Travis E. Jones, John Golden
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms offer a promising pathway for estimating the ground-state energies of periodic materials that are beyond the practical reach of classical electronic-structure methods. A remaining challenge is finite-size mitigation: quantum algorithms evaluate a finite supercell or finite Brillouin-zone mesh, while materials properties are defined in the thermodynamic limit. In this work we develop a quantum post-processing strategy for the leading two-body finite-size correction. After one-body shell effects are reduced by twist averaging, the dominant residual error is controlled by long-wavelength density fluctuations, which are encoded in the small-momentum static structure factor [MATH]. We formulate the corresponding operator in a Bloch-orbital basis, construct its block encoding through the density operator, and estimate its ground-state expectation value using an amplified Hadamard test. We also introduce adaptive global and local binary search procedures for identifying the infrared fitting window used to reconstruct the two-body finite size error correction. The resulting cost remains subleading relative to the main ground-state energy estimation routine: the structure-factor correction has leading [MATH] dependence on the Bloch-orbital basis size, avoids the large plane-wave prefactor of full Hamiltonian simulation, and requires only [MATH] logical qubits. This provides a fault-tolerant alternative to down-sampling, replacing repeated energy calculations on larger cells with targeted measurements of the infrared density correlations that control the finite-size effects.

motivation: Quantum algorithms for ground-state energy estimation of periodic materials suffer from finite-size effects; the thermodynamic limit requires corrections that are costly to compute classically.
method: The authors formulate the static structure factor operator in a Bloch-orbital basis, construct its block encoding via the density operator, and estimate its expectation value using an amplified Hadamard test with adaptive binary search for the infrared fitting window.
result: The cost of the structure-factor correction scales sublinearly relative to the main energy estimation routine, with O(N^2) dependence on basis size and O(log N) logical qubits, avoiding large plane-wave prefactors.
conclusion: This provides a fault-tolerant alternative to down-sampling for finite-size mitigation, replacing repeated energy calculations on larger cells with targeted measurements of infrared density correlations.

title: Bottleneck Effects And Harmonic-Type Velocity Bounds For Periodic Quantum Walks
authors: Houssam Abdul-Rahman, Thomas A. Jackson, Darren C. Ong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove explicit upper bounds on the propagation velocity of one-dimensional quantum walks with periodic coins of arbitrary period. We treat two complementary settings. First, in a perturbative regime where one transmission parameter is small, we show that the corresponding almost reflecting coin acts as a bottleneck for transport: the velocity is bounded linearly in this parameter, with an explicit leading order estimate. Second, for arbitrary nonzero transmission parameters, we prove a general a priori bound in terms of their harmonic mean, together with a refined version that detects the spatial variation of neighboring coins. Moreover, we prove a general lower bound on the velocity. These bounds apply directly to the corresponding CMV setting.
tldr: Proves velocity bounds for periodic quantum walks using bottleneck and harmonic mean arguments.
motivation: Understand transport limits in quantum walks with periodic coins, relevant to quantum information propagation.
method: Analytical bounds derived from transmission parameters and harmonic means, applied to CMV matrices.

Additionally, a general lower bound on the velocity is provided. The results are directly applicable to the corresponding CMV (Cantero-Moral-Velázquez) setting, which is a unitary representation of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

title: End-to-End Learning Of Quantum Control On Latent Dynamical Manifold
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong, Zong-Yuan Ge, Feng-Hua Ren, Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional quantum control relies on an iterative "simulate-then-optimize" paradigm, where dynamics simulation and control design are decoupled, leading to substantial computational overhead and limited scalability, particularly in noisy environments. Here, we propose an end-to-end quantum control framework based on long short-term memory, in which system dynamics and control strategies are learned jointly in a low dimensional latent manifold. The model directly maps initial states and environmental parameters to both dynamical trajectories and optimized control pulse in a single forward pass. The framework is validated on adiabatic speedup in a two-level system and state transfer in a one-dimensional spin chain under noise, achieving accurate dynamical prediction and control optimization. It improves the fidelity for both tasks and significantly reduces the optimization cost by three orders of magnitude compared with conventional iterative methods, while exhibiting strong generalization to multi-parameter, time-varying noise, as well as to different initial states and driving fields. Our work introduces a data-driven control paradigm based on latent manifold learning, reducing the computational bottleneck of iterative optimization and enabling real-time adaptive control of complex open quantum systems.

motivation: Traditional quantum control methods are computationally expensive and decouple simulation from optimization, limiting scalability and real-time adaptability.
method: The authors use a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to map initial states and noise parameters directly to dynamical trajectories and control pulses, learning a low-dimensional latent representation of the system.
result: The method achieves accurate prediction and control optimization, improving fidelity and reducing optimization cost by three orders of magnitude compared to iterative methods, with strong generalization to time-varying noise and different initial states.
conclusion: This data-driven approach offers a scalable and real-time alternative for quantum control, particularly in noisy open quantum systems.

title: Survivor-conditioned Renewal Laws And Observable Bounds For Open Intermittent Maps
authors: Jason Duvall
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent numerical computations and stochastic modeling by Brevitt and Klages suggest that introducing a hole in a Pomeau--Manneville map can suppress survivor-conditioned Lyapunov stretching. We prove a deterministic renewal theorem which explains this phenomenon and its observable-level generalizations. For an open intermittent map induced on a base away from the neutral fixed point, we describe the asymptotic distribution of the number of completed survivor returns to the base, conditioned on survival up to time [MATH]. The limiting law is expressed in terms of the killed induced transfer operator; for the conditionally invariant density of the killed induced system it is geometric. We then prove two reward results for additive observables. A reward domination theorem gives bounded survivor-conditioned Birkhoff sums, while a stronger final-tail asymptotic gives convergence to a finite limit. For generalized Pomeau--Manneville maps, bounded observables satisfying [MATH] near the neutral fixed point and a mild variation condition satisfy the domination hypotheses. When the neutral branch and final tails satisfy the corresponding regularity assumptions, asymptotically regular observables satisfy the convergence hypotheses. In particular, [MATH] gives bounded survivor-conditioned Lyapunov stretching for the generalized class; under these additional regularity assumptions, it converges. Under an additional entropy-domination assumption, we also derive a zero entropy-rate consequence for survivor return-length names and record the complementary linear growth of stretching when the hole contains a neighborhood of the neutral fixed point.
tldr: Proves renewal laws and observable bounds for open intermittent maps, focusing on survivor-conditioned Lyapunov stretching.
motivation: To explain numerical observations of suppressed Lyapunov stretching in Pomeau-Manneville maps with holes.
method: Uses deterministic renewal theory and killed induced transfer operators to derive asymptotic distributions and reward results.
result: Establishes a renewal theorem, reward domination, and final-tail convergence for bounded observables under regularity conditions.
conclusion: Provides rigorous justification for the suppression of survivor-conditioned Lyapunov stretching and generalizes to other observables.

The authors prove a deterministic renewal theorem that explains this suppression and its generalizations to other observables. They consider an open intermittent map induced on a base away from the neutral fixed point and describe the asymptotic distribution of the number of completed survivor returns to the base, conditioned on survival up to time t. The limiting law is expressed in terms of the killed induced transfer operator; for the conditionally invariant density of the killed induced system, it is geometric. Two reward results for additive observables are then proved: a reward domination theorem giving bounded survivor-conditioned Birkhoff sums, and a stronger final-tail asymptotic giving convergence to a finite limit. For generalized Pomeau–Manneville maps, bounded observables satisfying |ψ(x)| ≤ C x^γ near the neutral fixed point and a mild variation condition satisfy the domination hypotheses. When the neutral branch and final tails satisfy corresponding regularity assumptions, asymptotically regular observables satisfy the convergence hypotheses. In particular, ψ = log|f'| gives bounded survivor-conditioned Lyapunov stretching for the generalized class; under additional regularity assumptions, it converges. Under an entropy-domination assumption, a zero entropy-rate consequence for survivor return-length names is derived, and complementary linear growth of stretching when the hole contains a neighborhood of the neutral fixed point is recorded.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the protection of quantum steering ellipsoids from decoherence using non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but decoherence degrades them; understanding protection mechanisms is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids under non-Markovian noise, using master equations and geometric measures.
result: Non-Markovian environments can preserve the volume and shape of steering ellipsoids better than Markovian ones, depending on the noise parameters.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects can be harnessed to protect quantum steering correlations, which may benefit quantum communication protocols.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral properties.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique spectral degeneracies, but higher-order Liouvillian EPs in fermionic systems are not well understood.
method: Using third quantization formalism, the authors analytically characterize higher-order EPs in quadratic Liouvillians and study their signatures in dynamics.
result: They identify multiple EPs and show that an EP with the highest order governs the asymptotic dynamics, with observable effects in fermionic parity and correlation functions.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding higher-order EPs in dissipative fermionic systems, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.
method: Theoretical proposal using a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and induce nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: Achieves Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The atomtronic platform offers a controllable neutral-atom system for future quantum circuitry.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables control over nonclassical beams, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The proposed feedback control scheme may be useful for quantum information applications, but the paper is theoretical and lacks experimental validation.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Achilleas Lazarides and Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies apparent bistability in systems with weak long-range interactions, showing that such interactions can suppress defect nucleation and lead to metastable phases.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions affect phase coexistence and metastability is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a classical or quantum model with weak long-range interactions, likely using mean-field theory or numerical simulations to study defect dynamics and phase stability.
result: Weak long-range interactions can stabilize apparent bistability by suppressing the nucleation and growth of defects that would otherwise destroy one phase.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of interaction range in determining phase behavior, with implications for systems where long-range forces are present.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos

Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245427] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on geometry-dependent nonlinear electrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies.
method: The authors theoretically analyze second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures with different geometries, likely using nonlinear response theory or numerical simulations.
result: They find that the second-harmonic response is anisotropic and strongly dependent on the nanostructure geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear effects in superconducting circuits, which may inform design of quantum devices but does not directly address quantum information processing or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca and Balázs Dóra

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the self-energy in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain exhibits anomalous relaxation, indicating non-Fermi-liquid behavior even at high temperatures.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional systems is fundamental, and anomalous self-energy at zero temperature is known; this work extends the study to infinite temperature.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically and numerically for the Hubbard chain at infinite temperature using Bethe ansatz and other techniques.
result: They find that the self-energy decays as a power law in frequency, with an exponent that depends on interaction strength, signaling anomalous relaxation.
conclusion: The anomalous behavior persists at infinite temperature, suggesting that non-Fermi-liquid physics is not limited to low temperatures in 1D.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and complexity, but the paper focuses on a specific model (Ising on random graphs) without direct connection to thermodynamics or information theory.
method: The authors use spectral statistics (level spacing ratios) and out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) to probe chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs with varying connectivity.
result: They observe a crossover from localized to chaotic regimes as connectivity increases, and identify signatures of quantum chaos that are accessible on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos in disordered systems, but does not address thermodynamic constraints, information processing, or quantum speed limits.

tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase.
motivation: To understand universal scaling behavior in dissipative phase transitions to discrete time crystals.
method: Numerical simulations of an open quantum system model, analyzing defect density and transition delay as functions of quench time.
result: Observed power-law scaling of spatial defects and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism is universal for dissipative discrete time crystal formation, extending its applicability to open systems.

tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, focusing on a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universality in quantum many-body systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors analyze spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise using analytical and numerical methods, examining scaling behavior.
result: They find that noise modifies the crossover between monotonic and oscillatory decay, and identify universal scaling exponents.
conclusion: The results provide insight into noise-induced changes in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, relevant for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Nonuniversal Thermal Hall Responses In Fractional Quantum Hall Droplets

tldr: This paper computes thermal Hall conductance of fractional quantum Hall droplets beyond idealized edge theory, considering finite-size and self-energy effects.
motivation: To understand thermal Hall responses in realistic fractional quantum Hall systems, which are relevant for topological order and potential quantum information applications.
method: Analytical computation of thermal Hall conductance using edge theory with corrections from finite-size effects and quasihole self-energies.
result: The thermal Hall conductance deviates from universal quantized values due to nonuniversal corrections at low temperatures and finite sizes.
conclusion: Realistic fractional quantum Hall droplets exhibit nonuniversal thermal Hall responses, which must be accounted for in experiments and potential topological quantum computing applications.

Within the harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, the variational Gibbs free e…

motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in low-dimensional spin systems.

result: Identifies magnetoelastic signatures that distinguish thermal and quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: Magnetoelastic coupling provides a sensitive probe of phase transitions in deformable spin chains.

We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…

tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of random quantum circuits and their classical counterparts is important for quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates using mathematical proofs and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They show that under certain conditions, correlations decay to zero, indicating a loss of quantum or classical correlations.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the behavior of random circuits and may inform the design of quantum algorithms or error correction.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, leading to a violation of Ohm's addition law.
motivation: To explore nonreciprocal transport in thermoelectric systems driven by electron-phonon interactions, which could enable novel diode-like behavior.
method: The authors study a nanowire device with structural asymmetry and electron-phonon coupling, analyzing phonon emission and absorption asymmetries to derive nonreciprocal transport coefficients.
result: They find that the intrinsic nonreciprocity causes a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a fundamental mechanism for nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport, with potential applications in energy conversion and thermal management.

result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and extrapolative tool for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols

abstract:

tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for a simplified simulation that avoids tracking all intermediate error correlations.
result: The approach achieves polynomial-time simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: This work enables practical classical simulation of magic state preparation, which is important for verifying and optimizing fault-tolerant quantum computing protocols.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators enables rich nonequilibrium phenomena with potential for ultrafast control of material properties.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with noise exhibiting temporal correlations over many time scales (e.g., 1/f noise) is computationally challenging.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining conditions the process on a coarse realization, separating deterministic and bridge components, with ensemble averaging over bridges.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach offers practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proposes an efficient classical algorithm to compute the Neural Tangent Kernel of Clifford+Pauli quantum neural networks, showing they cannot achieve quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether wide quantum neural networks can provide a quantum advantage by analyzing their training dynamics via the Neural Tangent Kernel.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation of the circuit.
result: The algorithm computes the NTK and expected output of wide trained QNNs in polynomial time, proving that such networks are classically simulable.
conclusion: Wide quantum neural networks with Clifford+Pauli structure do not offer quantum advantage, as their training can be efficiently classically simulated.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of relaxation in stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom.
method: Experimental optical monitoring of field-induced birefringence combined with Smoluchowski equation modeling; polydispersity generates a spectrum of diffusion coefficients leading to multiscale relaxation.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation is observed and explained by polydispersity; sequential suppression of slow modes reduces relaxation time significantly.
conclusion: Memory effects in multiscale stochastic dynamics can be mitigated by mode-suppression protocols, providing a strategy for controlling relaxation in complex systems.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the complexity-theoretic foundations of BosonSampling to the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving hardness for approximate sampling.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime (many more modes than photons), but experimental demonstrations operate in a saturated regime with comparable numbers of modes and photons. The gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new anticoncentration bounds and use random matrix theory to show that the output distribution of linear-optical circuits in the saturated regime is sufficiently complex to be hard to sample classically, assuming standard conjectures.
result: They prove that approximate BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is #P-hard under plausible complexity assumptions, and provide evidence that the distribution is anticoncentrated.
conclusion: The results validate that current photonic quantum advantage experiments in the saturated regime are on solid complexity-theoretic ground, reinforcing the case for quantum supremacy in photonics.

authors: M. Frómeta Fernández

title: Floquet Topological State Induced By Light-driven Band Inversion In SnTe
authors: F. Chassot
A. Pulkkinen
G. Kremer
C. Wang
J. Schusser
J. Krempaský

G. Springholz
