abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Femtosecond light pulses induce a transient topological state in SnTe via band inversion.
motivation: To demonstrate light-induced topological phase transitions in a semiconductor, which has been theoretically predicted but lacked clear experimental evidence.
method: Pump-probe photoemission spectroscopy on SnTe thin films excited by femtosecond laser pulses, tracking band structure changes.
result: Transient band inversion and emergence of topological surface states are observed, confirming a Floquet topological state.
conclusion: Light-driven band engineering can create topological states in equilibrium trivial semiconductors, opening avenues for ultrafast topological switching.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the interplay of correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion.
result: They identify conditions under which ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic order is favored.
conclusion: Quantum geometry plays a key role in determining magnetic ground states in narrow-band systems.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a 1D non-Hermitian chain model and analyze its spectral and localization properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization transitions as parameters vary.
conclusion: The work extends understanding of non-Hermitian physics, particularly symmetry and localization, in one-dimensional systems.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

Moiré superlattices (MSLs) in van der Waals heterostructures have demonstrated their incredible power in driving emergent electronic phenomena, some of which are reminiscent of those usually only observed in bulk strongly correlated quantum materials. With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on flat-band driven electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent strongly correlated electronic phases, and understanding Kondo physics in these systems may reveal new quantum states.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo lattice model in a moiré superlattice with flat bands.
result: They find that flat bands can drive a Kondo breakdown transition and lead to reentrant heavy-fermion behavior as a function of doping or temperature.
conclusion: The work highlights the rich interplay between flat-band geometry and strong correlations in moiré systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that orbital magnetization can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a physical observable that directly probes multiband topology beyond the usual single-band Chern number.
method: Decompose orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and relate them to topological invariants.
result: The decomposition allows extraction of multiband topological invariants from magnetization responses.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, offering a new experimental signature.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, and Ruifeng Lu

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: To understand the microscopic dynamics of doublon-holon pairs in strongly correlated systems under strong laser fields.
method: Exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain.
result: The doublon population dynamics are linked to high-harmonic generation spectra.
conclusion: The work provides insight into non-equilibrium dynamics in Mott insulators but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:
Author(s): Ensuo Ma and Zhi Song

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics with dissipation.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals, using a 1D ladder model as a parameter space analog.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D ladder, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D semimetals.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional lines to lower-dimensional systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and long-range hopping in topological insulators.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and analyzes topological invariants and edge states.
result: Finds that Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping modify the topological phase diagram and domain wall states.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass
abstract:
Author(s): João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, and T. Grass

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. Here, the authors study a microscopic ladder model featuring both diagonal hopping pathways and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions. They demonstrate that while both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior, they stabilize completely distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241119] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies controlled pairing symmetries in a Fermi-Hubbard ladder with band flattening, focusing on competing pairing mechanisms and their spatial patterns.
motivation: To understand how slow electrons and competing interactions can stabilize distinct superconducting states in systems like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.
method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting pairing symmetries.
result: They find that diagonal hopping and loop exchange independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms.

title: Differentiable Learning And Control Of Free-energy-driven Pattern Dynamics
authors: Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, And Martin Z. Bazant

Author(s): Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, and Martin Z. Bazant

Pattern-forming dynamics govern the behavior of many quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems, yet learning and controlling the corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) models on realistic geometries remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified, differentiable framework …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023344] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A differentiable framework for learning and controlling pattern-forming PDEs in soft-matter and electrochemical systems.
motivation: Pattern-forming dynamics are important in many physical systems, but learning and controlling PDE models on realistic geometries is challenging.
method: Develops a unified differentiable framework combining neural networks and adjoint methods to learn and control free-energy-driven pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates effective learning and control of pattern formation in several examples, including electrochemical and soft-matter systems.
conclusion: The framework enables data-driven discovery and control of pattern-forming PDEs, with potential applications in materials science and engineering.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model dynamics.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work compares various classical numerical approaches to assess their accuracy and efficiency.
method: Applies a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of the performance and limitations of each method for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific regime and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, demonstrating that disorder can drive topological phases not present in clean systems.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can induce new topological phases in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, beyond those achievable in clean systems.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a Chern insulator coupled to local magnetic moments with strong directional disorder, and analyze the resulting topological phases using numerical methods.
result: They find that strong disorder gives rise to topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in any clean system.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering novel topological phases in Chern insulators, expanding the possibilities for topological matter.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor to simulate driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally show a utilizable quantum advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses a 61-atom ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system and quantify computational advantage via cross-entropy benchmarking.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage by outperforming classical simulations in sampling from the output distribution.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform can serve as a viable quantum simulator for demonstrating quantum advantage in many-body physics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, challenging the thermodynamic limit assumption.
motivation: To understand how geometry-induced quantum phase separation affects the thermodynamic limit in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models and analyze the effect of domain shape on ground states using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and anyon permutations.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a symmetry, which is important for understanding topological phases and dualities.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants: a homomorphism to anyon permutation symmetries and a generalized GNVW index, and shows equivalence to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, with examples including the Kramers-Wannier duality mapping to anyon permutation in toric code.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are classified by anyon permutation and index, and cannot always be extended to full QCAs, mixing nontrivially with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in lossy atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify realistic gains under lossy conditions.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering. One-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated for phase sensitivity.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature significantly reduces benefits.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic losses, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed to realize gains.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: This paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into shape invariants and bosonic excitations, applied to the lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of the wave function into fixed invariants (shapes) satisfying the Pauli principle and a variable bosonic part.
result: A benchmark lithium wave function with hundreds of basis functions is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five of which are numerically significant.
conclusion: The decomposition reveals superselection rules in configuration space and aids in finding robust entangled states.

title: Multi-parameter Two-photon Polarimetry At The Quantum Limit
authors: Joseph Niblo, Luca Maggio, Russell M. J. Brooks, Joseph Ho, Vincenzo Tamma, Alessandro Fedrizzi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic quantum metrology has demonstrated advantages in precision and resource efficiency for a wide range of applications, with several schemes approaching the fundamental quantum Cram\'er-Rao precision bound (QCRB). However, the intrinsic incompatibility of quantum measurements represents a hurdle in extending these advantages to the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. In this paper, we present an experimental protocol approaching the QCRB simultaneously in two polarisation parameters, across a wide range of the parameter space, with as few as [MATH] photon pairs, offering advantages for polarimetric sensing for dim sources such as in X-ray astronomy or photosensitive samples.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of multi-parameter two-photon polarimetry approaching the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Extend quantum metrology advantages to simultaneous estimation of multiple polarization parameters, relevant for dim sources like X-ray astronomy.
method: Uses entangled photon pairs and a tailored measurement protocol to achieve near-optimal precision for two polarization parameters.
result: Approaches the quantum Cramér-Rao bound simultaneously for both parameters across a wide parameter range with few photon pairs.
conclusion: Demonstrates practical multi-parameter quantum polarimetry at the quantum limit, with potential applications in low-light polarimetric sensing.

title: Universal Framework For The Design Of Near-zero Refractive Index Photonic Crystals
authors: Micha\"el Lobet Adrien Debacq
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-zero-index (NZI) media are of great interest for controlling light-matter interactions, but homogeneous NZI materials in the telecom band remain limited and often suffer from significant losses. Photonic crystals provide an attractive alternative due to their tunability and use of low-loss constituent materials. This work presents a predictive framework for designing epsilon-near-zero (ENZ), mu-near-zero (MNZ), and epsilon-and-mu-near-zero (EMNZ) photonic crystals. We demonstrate an equivalence between Dirac cones and EMNZ behavior, showing that a Dirac cone at the Gamma point is both necessary and sufficient to obtain an effective EMNZ response under normal incidence. This result implies that the presence of a Dirac cone fully determines the NZI response of a photonic crystal, independent of the material composition. The prediction is based on mode symmetry universality and effective medium theory. The approach enables switching between ENZ-MNZ and EMNZ regimes through geometric tuning of the unit cell. It is validated on triangular and rectangular lattices. Overall, this work provides a predictive design strategy for NZI photonic crystals, replacing trial-and-error optimization. It may also impact metamaterials in the telecom regime and applications in quantum communication.
tldr: A predictive framework for designing near-zero-index photonic crystals using Dirac cones and effective medium theory.
motivation: Homogeneous near-zero-index materials suffer from losses and limited availability; photonic crystals offer a tunable, low-loss alternative but lack a systematic design approach.
method: The authors establish an equivalence between Dirac cones at the Gamma point and epsilon-and-mu-near-zero (EMNZ) behavior under normal incidence, using mode symmetry and effective medium theory, and validate on triangular and rectangular lattices.
result: Dirac cones are both necessary and sufficient for EMNZ response; geometric tuning enables switching between ENZ, MNZ, and EMNZ regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a predictive design strategy for NZI photonic crystals, potentially impacting telecom metamaterials and quantum communication applications.

title: I-QMapper: Error-Aware Layout Optimization And Device Diagnostics For Nisq Hardware
authors: Kenneth Merz Milana Bazayeva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving high-fidelity execution on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware requires careful selection of physical qubit layouts, as gate errors, readout errors, and coherence times vary across the device and drift over time. Currently, qubit mapping is performed either through manual inspection of device calibration data or through automated layout pipelines, neither of which provides integrated, interactive layout visualization combined with calibration analytics. In this work, we present the Interactive Quantum Mapper (I-QMapper), a Jupyter-based, open-source tool for noise-aware layout selection, visualization, and analysis on superconducting quantum hardware. I-QMapper offers two operating modes: a general-purpose mode for arbitrary circuits, and a dedicated mode for quantum-chemistry applications, specifically tailored to the Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) ansatz. Within each mode, a Design panel supports interactive layout construction, while an Error panel provides calibration analytics through four temporal viewing modes (Live, Snapshot, Intraday, and Multi-day range) together with threshold filtering and delta-mode comparison for drift identification. Each layout receives a Layout-Quality Score (LQS) that aggregates the readout and two-qubit gate errors of the layout into a single quality value. Starting from the automatic LUCJ circuit-generation provided by IBM Quantum, we extend it to a multi-programming setting in which multiple circuits are mapped onto a single quantum processing unit (QPU). I-QMapper further supports side-by-side visualization of two quantum backends and layout comparison, and session export for experimental reproducibility. By combining interactive exploration with calibration analytics, I-QMapper aims to support both rapid layout prototyping and informed noise-aware experimental design on NISQ devices.
tldr: I-QMapper is a Jupyter-based tool for noise-aware qubit layout selection and visualization on NISQ hardware, with integrated calibration analytics.
motivation: Current qubit mapping methods lack integrated, interactive layout visualization combined with calibration analytics, making it difficult to achieve high-fidelity execution on noisy hardware.
method: The tool provides two operating modes (general-purpose and quantum-chemistry), an interactive Design panel for layout construction, an Error panel with temporal viewing modes and threshold filtering, and a Layout-Quality Score aggregating readout and two-qubit gate errors.
result: I-QMapper enables rapid layout prototyping, drift identification, side-by-side backend comparison, and session export for reproducibility.
conclusion: The tool supports noise-aware experimental design on NISQ devices but does not present new theoretical or algorithmic contributions to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Su(1,1) Symmetry And Exact Solutions Of The Dunkl-Klein-Gordon Equation In Higher Dimensions
authors: M. Salazar-Ram\'irez, B. C. L\"utf\"uo\u{g}lu, Jes\'us Alfredo Mart\'inez-Nu\~no
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the [MATH]-dimensional Dunkl--Klein--Gordon equation for a scalar particle within an algebraic framework. By employing Schr\"odinger factorization, we construct the generators of the [MATH] algebra and establish the associated symmetry of the radial sector. The energy spectrum is derived using irreducible unitary representations, and the corresponding Sturmian radial basis is obtained analytically. We analyze the [MATH]-dimensional Dunkl--Klein--Gordon oscillator and the bound-state sector of the [MATH]-dimensional Dunkl--Klein--Gordon equation with a Dunkl--Coulomb-like potential. Furthermore, [MATH] coherent states are constructed and their time evolution is analyzed, revealing a characteristic radial oscillation behavior. The results show that the Dunkl deformation introduces parity-dependent modifications in the spatial structure of the system while preserving its underlying algebraic dynamics.
tldr: The paper studies the Dunkl-Klein-Gordon equation in higher dimensions using SU(1,1) algebraic methods, deriving exact solutions and coherent states.
motivation: To understand the effects of Dunkl deformation (parity-dependent modifications) on relativistic quantum systems with underlying algebraic symmetry.
method: Schrödinger factorization is used to construct SU(1,1) generators; irreducible unitary representations yield the energy spectrum; coherent states are built and their time evolution analyzed.
result: Exact solutions for the Dunkl-Klein-Gordon oscillator and Coulomb-like potential are obtained; coherent states exhibit radial oscillations with parity-dependent spatial structure.
conclusion: The Dunkl deformation preserves algebraic dynamics while introducing parity-dependent modifications, extending the algebraic approach to deformed relativistic equations.

title: Quantum Dynamic Time Warping For Multivariate Time Series Classification
authors: Diego Alvarez-Estevez, Alejandro Mayorga-Redondo, Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a cornerstone for time series classification, but its reliance on Euclidean distances fails to capture latent cross-channel correlations in complex multivariate data. We propose a hybrid Quantum Dynamic Time Warping (qDTW) architecture, replacing the classical distance metric with the parameterized geometry of a quantum Hilbert space. Through structural ablation on benchmarks up to [MATH] spatial dimensions, we establish fundamental topological rules for quantum sequence alignment. We introduce a Unified Pre-Embedding Adjoint Ansatz that decouples trainable entanglement from classical data, eliminating the severe phase-scrambling and information bottlenecks inherent to traditional measurements. We demonstrate this decoupled architecture allows untrained quantum kernels to act as highly expressive baselines, while parameterized training effectively untangles deeply overlapping hyper-dimensional data. Furthermore, we identify a strict spatial-temporal expressivity tradeoff: temporal depth (data re-uploading) is necessary for dimensionally restricted univariate circuits, but applying it to wide multi-qubit registers triggers chaotic frequency-spectrum explosions and representation collapse. By navigating these topological hazards, our multivariate quantum architecture outperforms classical baselines, setting a new standard for integrating parameterized quantum circuits with dynamic programming.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for multivariate time series classification using quantum dynamic time warping.
motivation: Classical DTW fails to capture cross-channel correlations in multivariate time series; quantum Hilbert space geometry may provide a more expressive metric.
method: Replaces Euclidean distance in DTW with a parameterized quantum kernel, using a Unified Pre-Embedding Adjoint Ansatz to decouple entanglement from classical data.
result: Identifies a spatial-temporal expressivity tradeoff and shows that the quantum architecture outperforms classical baselines on benchmarks.
conclusion: Parameterized quantum circuits can enhance dynamic programming for time series classification, but careful design is needed to avoid representation collapse.

title: Vibrational High-harmonics And Period-doubling Bifurcation Probed By Time-resolved Electron Diffraction
authors: Alexander Schr\"oder, Kai Nettersheim, Ferdinand Evers, Sascha Sch\"afer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanoscale mechanical oscillators exhibit a plethora of nonlinear phenomena with promising applications for the sensing and clocking of processes down to atomic length scales. Oscillator dynamics are typically probed by electrical or optical means, providing only limited access to the spatial profile of the oscillator motion. Here, we introduce event-based convergent beam electron diffraction for the spatio-temporal mapping of nanoscale mechanical resonators in ultrafast transmission electron microscopy. Employing an optically driven silicon membrane resonator at various driving strengths, we gain access to nonlinear processes with increasing complexity, ranging from a simple Duffing behavior to nonlinear multimode coupling and period-doubling bifurcations. The time-resolved diffraction probing approach supports a spatial resolution down to a few nanometers and a temporal resolution of 5 ns and provides quantitative information on the local membrane bending. Because the diffraction signal responds to local displacement gradients, which become more pronounced as resonators shrink, this approach offers a route toward probing nonlinear nanomechanics at the atomic scale.
tldr: This paper uses time-resolved electron diffraction to probe nonlinear dynamics in nanomechanical resonators, including high-harmonics and period-doubling bifurcations.
motivation: To achieve spatio-temporal mapping of nanoscale mechanical oscillators with high spatial resolution, enabling study of nonlinear phenomena at the atomic scale.
method: Event-based convergent beam electron diffraction in ultrafast transmission electron microscopy is applied to an optically driven silicon membrane resonator.
result: The technique resolves Duffing behavior, nonlinear multimode coupling, and period-doubling bifurcations with 5 ns temporal and few-nanometer spatial resolution.
conclusion: This diffraction-based approach offers a route to probing nonlinear nanomechanics at atomic length scales, with potential applications in sensing and clocking.

title: Fast-Mixing Markov Chains Without Gradients
authors: Robert Scheichl Robert Kutri
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most approaches for accelerating Markov chain mixing either rely on incorporating expensive geometric information in the proposals, or reduce the per-step cost of sampling via surrogate densities. We propose a localisation principle that allows a surrogate-based Metropolis-Hastings proposal to exploit gradient-level geometric information of the target density, without evaluating either the target gradient or the surrogate gradient. The construction relies on regularisation and tempering of the proposal measure. We show that the expected proposal displacement coincides with the Langevin drift up to controlled error. The resulting framework, Delayed Acceptance with Regularisation and Tempering (DART), achieves an [MATH] mixing time from warm start for strongly log-concave targets with condition number [MATH] in [MATH] dimensions. This matches the known [MATH] rate for MALA when [MATH], and scales as [MATH], independent of dimension, otherwise. This is, to our knowledge, the first mixing time guarantee for a surrogate-transition-based MCMC method. We demonstrate DART on a hierarchical spatial generalised linear mixed model. In this setting, the Dirichlet-Neumann averaging parametrisation, originally introduced for the efficient simulation of Gaussian processes, is repurposed to supply the surrogate, and its linear memory and log-linear arithmetic scaling in the number of observation sites carry over to inference.
tldr: A surrogate-based MCMC method that accelerates mixing without gradient evaluations, achieving fast mixing for strongly log-concave targets.
motivation: Standard MCMC methods either require expensive gradient computations or suffer from slow mixing; the authors aim to combine the benefits of surrogate models with gradient-like information without explicit gradient evaluations.
method: They propose Delayed Acceptance with Regularisation and Tempering (DART), which uses a regularized and tempered surrogate proposal to approximate the Langevin drift, enabling a Metropolis-Hastings step that avoids gradient computations.
result: DART achieves O(κ^2 log(1/ε)) mixing time for strongly log-concave targets with condition number κ, matching MALA when κ=O(1) and scaling as O(κ^2) independent of dimension otherwise.
conclusion: DART provides the first mixing time guarantee for surrogate-transition-based MCMC, demonstrating practical efficiency on a hierarchical spatial GLMM.

title: Deriving Approximate Message Passing From The Convex Gaussian Min-Max Theorem
authors: Babak Hassibi Vikrant Malik
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximate message passing (AMP) provides fast iterative algorithms for high-dimensional signal recovery with Gaussian design matrices, while the Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) gives a static optimization framework for obtaining sharp asymptotic characterizations of convex estimators. Although these two frameworks often lead to the same scalar state-evolution equations, their connection is usually indirect. In this paper, we establish a direct connection between the two for regularized linear regression in the proportional high-dimensional regime. When the CGMT Auxiliary Optimization (AO) and Primary Optimization (PO) give the same primal-dual solution, we show that the CGMT framework recovers the AMP fixed-point equations, including the Onsager correction. We further identify the AO Gaussian vectors with the Gaussian perturbations in the primal and residual AMP channels. For regularized M-estimation, the same viewpoint recovers the fixed point of scalar-variance max-sum Generalized AMP (GAMP). These results show that the AMP (and GAMP) iterations are suggested, and can be derived, from the CGMT framework, and may further suggest a way to derive AMP-like algorithms in settings where CGMT applies but standard AMP derivations are unavailable.
tldr: This paper establishes a direct connection between approximate message passing (AMP) and the convex Gaussian min-max theorem (CGMT) for high-dimensional signal recovery.
motivation: AMP and CGMT are two powerful frameworks for analyzing high-dimensional statistical problems, but their relationship was previously indirect. The authors aim to unify them.
method: The authors show that when the CGMT auxiliary and primary optimizations yield the same primal-dual solution, the CGMT framework recovers the AMP fixed-point equations, including the Onsager correction. They also extend this to generalized AMP.
result: The CGMT framework can directly derive AMP iterations, providing a new perspective on AMP's state evolution and suggesting a way to derive AMP-like algorithms in settings where CGMT applies.
conclusion: This work bridges two important theoretical frameworks, potentially enabling the derivation of new AMP algorithms for problems where standard AMP derivations are unavailable.

title: Differential Privacy Over Hamming Codes
authors: Morteza Varasteh Borzoo Rassouli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the transmission of the outputs of counting queries over a binary symmetric channel (BSC), where Hamming codes are employed as the channel encoder. Since the channel is inherently noisy, this transmission already provides a degree of privacy protection ``for free'', albeit at the cost of reduced utility in the form of decoding errors. A natural question is whether this privacy can be further improved (i) without any additional real-time obfuscation of the data, such as injecting artificial noise prior to transmission, and (ii) without increasing the end-to-end error probability. In this work, we answer this question in the affirmative by deriving an optimal codeword arrangement that strictly improves differential privacy guarantees while incurring no real-time computational overhead and no degradation in utility.
tldr: This paper improves differential privacy guarantees for counting queries transmitted over a binary symmetric channel by optimally arranging Hamming codewords, without adding noise or increasing error probability.
motivation: To enhance privacy in data transmission without sacrificing utility or requiring additional real-time obfuscation.
method: Derives an optimal codeword arrangement for Hamming codes that minimizes the worst-case privacy leakage under differential privacy metrics.
result: The proposed arrangement strictly improves differential privacy guarantees while maintaining the same end-to-end error probability and no extra computational overhead.
conclusion: Privacy can be improved for free by exploiting the inherent noise of the channel and careful code design, with no trade-off in utility.

title: Prone: Petrov-Galerkin Operator Learning Unifies Dmd, SINDy & Koopmanism
authors: Matthew J. Colbrook, April Herwig, J. Nathan Kutz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven dynamics often asks how to linearize a nonlinear system. We ask instead: which observables should be advanced, and where should their futures live? This leads to Petrov Regression Of Nonlinear Evolution (PRONE), a Petrov--Galerkin regression framework based on [MATH] with distinct trial and test dictionaries. In this form, DMD, EDMD, SINDy, Koopman regression, sparse regression, and low-rank regression become variants of one construction: different dictionaries, weights, and constraints. We keep the linear algebra of Koopman learning, but drop the artificial requirement that a finite model map a dictionary into itself. With this asymmetry, eigenmodes are no longer the right objects. Instead, we use singular modes, which identify the observable combinations captured by the data, their projected futures, and the strength of the coupling between the two spaces. We identify the limiting projected operator and prove [MATH] convergence of the resulting nonlinear predictor. We give examples from chaotic maps, the double gyre, a pitching-airfoil wake, and Lorenz--63, where PRONE outperforms DeepONets, Fourier neural operators, and reservoir computers with considerably fewer parameters. These examples show the same message: lift once, regress once, and let the singular structure reveal statistics, transport, prediction, and dimension.
tldr: PRONE is a Petrov-Galerkin regression framework for data-driven dynamics that unifies DMD, SINDy, and Koopman methods by using distinct trial and test dictionaries.
motivation: To linearize nonlinear systems without requiring the finite model to map a dictionary into itself, enabling more flexible and accurate predictions.
method: The method uses Petrov-Galerkin regression with separate trial and test dictionaries, employing singular modes instead of eigenmodes to identify observable combinations and their projected futures.
result: PRONE outperforms DeepONets, Fourier neural operators, and reservoir computers on chaotic maps, double gyre, pitching-airfoil wake, and Lorenz-63, with fewer parameters.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified perspective on several data-driven methods and demonstrates superior performance on benchmark problems.

title: The Quantum Instrument Monad
authors: Tobias Fritz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monads are a ubiquitous structure in functional programming used for modelling computational effects. For example, the state monad models the effect of a computation interacting with a memory system. Here we introduce the quantum instrument monad [MATH], which models the effect of a computation interacting with a quantum system with algebra of observables [MATH]. It can be thought of as a noncommutative generalization of the state monad. We construct this quantum instrument monad in two versions: a finitary version on the category of sets and a measure-theoretic version on the category of measurable spaces (the latter under the assumption that [MATH] is a type I von Neumann algebra with separable predual). Both versions are strong monads. The construction of the measure-theoretic version is based on a new notion of integral of a quantum-operation-valued function against a state-valued measure.
tldr: Introduces a monad for modeling quantum measurements and instruments in functional programming, generalizing the state monad to noncommutative algebras.
motivation: To provide a categorical framework for quantum computational effects, enabling compositional reasoning about quantum measurements and instruments.
method: Constructs the quantum instrument monad in two versions: finitary on sets and measure-theoretic on measurable spaces, using integrals of quantum-operation-valued functions against state-valued measures.
result: Both versions are strong monads, and the measure-theoretic version works for type I von Neumann algebras with separable predual.
conclusion: The quantum instrument monad offers a formal tool for modeling quantum effects in functional programming, but its practical impact on quantum information or thermodynamics is unclear.

motivation: Understanding edge reconstruction in quantum spin Hall insulators is important for characterizing topological phases and their stability under interactions.
method: The authors use real-space density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) in both grand-canonical and canonical ensembles to study the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions.
result: They observe interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulator.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay of interactions and topology in quantum spin Hall insulators, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultrafast Magneto-Optical Fingerprints Of Altermagnetism In MnTe
authors: Xu Yang, Xingkai Cheng, Zhuo Deng, Yu-Han Gao, Qing-Lin Yang, Zheng Chang, Peng-Tao Yang, Hong-Mei Feng, Xiang-Qun Zhang, Wei He, Junwei Liu, And Zhao-Hua Cheng
abstract:

Recently identified altermagnets exhibit a distinctive dual-space nature: they possess spin-split electronic bands akin to ferromagnets in momentum space while maintaining the fully compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets in real space. This inherent duality, originating from the same crystal …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256702] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports ultrafast magneto-optical fingerprints of altermagnetism in MnTe, a condensed matter physics study of a novel magnetic phase.
motivation: Altermagnets are a recently identified class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization, and their ultrafast dynamics are unexplored.
method: The authors use time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE) spectroscopy to probe the spin dynamics in MnTe thin films.
result: They observe distinct ultrafast magneto-optical signatures that are attributed to the altermagnetic order, including a characteristic temperature dependence.
conclusion: The findings establish ultrafast magneto-optics as a tool to identify and study altermagnetism, opening a new direction in condensed matter physics.

title: Hearing The Light: Stray-Field Noise From The Emergent Photon In Quantum Spin Ice
authors: Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, And Chris R. Laumann
abstract:

Decisive experimental confirmation of the U(1) quantum spin liquid phase in quantum spin ice remains an outstanding challenge. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256705] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes stray-field magnetometry to detect emergent photons in quantum spin ice, a U(1) quantum spin liquid.
motivation: Experimental confirmation of U(1) quantum spin liquids remains challenging; the paper aims to provide a direct probe of the emergent photon excitation.
method: Theoretical analysis of stray-field noise from emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice, using magnetometry as a detection tool.
result: Stray-field magnetometry can directly detect the gapless photon excitation, offering a signature of the quantum spin liquid phase.
conclusion: Stray-field magnetometry is a viable experimental probe for emergent photons in quantum spin ice, aiding in the confirmation of U(1) quantum spin liquids.

title: Close Proximity To A Quantum Phase Transition In ${\mathrm{TmZn}}_{2}{\mathrm{GaO}}_{5}$
authors: Matthew Ennis, Rabindranath Bag, Tessa Cookmeyer, Matthew B. Stone, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Tao Hong, Leon Balents, And Sara Haravifard

tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a triangular lattice magnet TmZn2GaO5, which exhibits a quantum phase with strong Ising anisotropy and a gapped excitation, suggesting proximity to a quantum phase transition.
motivation: To discover and understand new quantum phases in frustrated magnets, particularly triangular lattice systems with Ising anisotropy.
method: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic measurements on single crystals of TmZn2GaO5, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The material shows a pseudodoublet ground state, strong Ising anisotropy, and a low-energy gapped excitation at the M point, indicating proximity to a quantum phase transition.
conclusion: TmZn2GaO5 is a promising platform for studying quantum criticality and exotic phases in frustrated magnets.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. In contrast to standard Poincaré sphere analogs that are restricted to subspaces, this parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities where a mode amplitude vanishes.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, which is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To provide a complete parametrization of three-state optical modes beyond standard Poincaré sphere analogs.
method: An octant geometric framework mapping higher-order optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus.
result: The parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified geometric representation for higher-order optical modes.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, and Shi-Hai Dong

Quantum image processing relies on the efficient encoding of classical image data into quantum states, yet the practical performance of existing encoding schemes on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware remains insufficiently understood. Most prior studies have emphasized asymptotic resou…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062456] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum image encoding schemes on NISQ devices, focusing on noise resilience and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum image processing requires efficient encoding of classical images into quantum states, but the performance of existing encodings on noisy hardware is not well understood.
method: The authors implement and compare several encoding schemes (e.g., FRQI, NEQR, QPIE) on simulated and real NISQ devices, measuring fidelity, circuit depth, and noise resilience.
result: They find that simpler encodings like QPIE are more noise-resilient but less expressive, while more complex encodings suffer from higher error rates on current hardware.
conclusion: The choice of encoding must balance expressiveness and noise tolerance for practical NISQ applications.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes displacement detection for arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation, focusing on precision sensing.
motivation: To improve sensitivity of optically levitated sensors for force, acceleration, and torque measurements by considering nonspherical geometries.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the scattered field and detection efficiency using Rayleigh-Gans theory and numerical simulations for arbitrary shapes.
result: They find that optimal detection can be achieved by matching the detection mode to the scattered field, with significant improvements for certain shapes.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for designing optimal detection schemes for levitated optomechanics with nonspherical particles, enhancing sensor performance.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Hubenschmid and Victor Rueskov Christiansen

The theoretical description of broadband, multimode quantum pulses undergoing a second-order [MATH]-nonlinear interaction can be quite intricate due to the large dimensionality of the underlying phase space. However, in many cases only a few broadband (temporal) modes are relevant before and af…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063734] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a phase-space formalism for broadband multimode quantum pulses undergoing second-order nonlinear interactions, focusing on open-system dynamics.
motivation: Describing broadband multimode quantum pulses in nonlinear media is complex due to high dimensionality; the authors aim to simplify by identifying relevant temporal modes.
method: They use a phase-space approach (e.g., Wigner function) to model open-system dynamics of second-order nonlinear interactions, incorporating loss and decoherence.
result: The formalism reduces the problem to a few effective modes and provides equations for the evolution of the quantum state under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The work enables efficient simulation of quantum optical systems with nonlinearities and loss, relevant for quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

Time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is a central tool for studying the dynamical electronic structure of molecules and solids, yet aspects of its mathematical foundations remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we revisit the foundations of TDDFT within a finite-dimensional sett…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062222] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) are not fully understood, especially for finite-dimensional systems.
method: The authors reformulate the time-dependent Schrödinger equation as a constrained Hamiltonian system on a Grassmann manifold, using geometric mechanics and symplectic reduction.
result: They derive a rigorous framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, including existence and uniqueness of solutions, and provide numerical examples.
conclusion: The geometric approach clarifies the mathematical structure of TDDFT and may lead to improved numerical methods for electronic structure calculations.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062816] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers, focusing on isotope shift effects.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, limiting precision.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous polarization on the measured signal.
result: They quantify how inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization leads to systematic errors in gyroscope and comagnetometer readings.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating these errors is crucial for improving the accuracy of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions

tldr: This paper studies ground-state structures of inhomogeneous population-imbalanced Fermi gases with pairing interactions using Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization affect phase coexistence in quasi-one-dimensional Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory to analyze ground-state structures of two-component atomic Fermi gases in box potentials with spatially varying profiles.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases in real space and characterize their properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into inhomogeneous Fermi gases but is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:

motivation: To demonstrate a compact, chip-based atom interferometer for precision measurements.
method: A thermal cloud of Rb-87 atoms is magnetically trapped on a chip, and a state-selective spatial splitting of internal states is used to realize a Ramsey interferometer.
result: The interferometer is successfully realized, showing interference fringes.
conclusion: Atom-chip interferometers can be built with thermal clouds, offering a compact platform for interferometry.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè

tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments on ring superfluids with barriers or impurities motivate a theoretical analysis of stability in more general configurations.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach to study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential.
result: They find that the rotating necklace potential can increase the stability of the superfluid compared to static barriers, extending the regime of stable flow.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling superfluid stability using rotating potentials, relevant for ultracold atom experiments.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons from bulk crystals suffer from mode mismatch that degrades performance.
method: The authors develop a spatial-spectral mode analysis of the SPDC process, modeling the coupling of the down-converted fields into Gaussian fiber modes and computing the resulting joint spectral intensity and heralding efficiency.
result: They find that optimal fiber coupling requires balancing the phase-matching conditions and pump focusing to achieve high heralding efficiency and spectral purity simultaneously, with trade-offs quantified.
conclusion: The analysis provides design guidelines for SPDC sources to achieve high-performance fiber-coupled photon pairs, but the work is primarily an engineering optimization without fundamental quantum information or thermodynamic insights.

title: Bistable Fourth Sound Resonance In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}\text{−}\mathrm{B}$ Due To Gap Suppression

tldr: This paper studies bistable fourth sound resonance in superfluid 3He-B due to gap suppression, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: To understand nonlinear acoustic phenomena in superfluid 3He-B arising from order parameter suppression.
method: Experimental measurement of fourth sound resonance in a superfluid 3He-B cavity, analyzing nonlinear response and bistability.
result: Observation of bistable resonance behavior attributed to gap suppression by the sound field.
conclusion: The bistability provides insight into the nonlinear dynamics of superfluid 3He-B and its order parameter.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain
authors: Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang

motivation: BCS wave functions under open boundary conditions are nontrivial but important for understanding edge properties of topological superconductors.
method: The authors derive the exact many-body wave function using a Bogoliubov transformation and solve the resulting BdG equations for the open chain.
result: They obtain an explicit form of the ground-state wave function and compute the edge magnetization, revealing topological edge modes.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for an open superconducting chain, clarifying the relationship between bulk topology and edge magnetism.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$

motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, specifically the anomalous and topological Hall effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall resistivity and magnetization, and analysis using Berry curvature concepts.
result: Observation of large anomalous Hall conductivity and a topological Hall effect arising from the non-coplanar spin structure.
conclusion: The kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6 is a promising platform for studying topological transport phenomena.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism

tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetism via antiferroelastic lattice distortion, enabling reversible switching of spin splitting without net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnets offer spin splitting without net magnetization, but nonvolatile control of their spin states is needed for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic strain can switch the altermagnetic order parameter in a model material.
result: They find that strain-driven antiferroelastic distortion reversibly flips the momentum-space spin splitting, providing a nonvolatile switching mechanism.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway for electrically or mechanically controlling altermagnetic states, advancing altermagnet-based spintronics.

title: Spin Transfer Torque Induced Deterministic Néel Vector Switching In Altermagnets

motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications; understanding spin-transfer torque in them is crucial for device development.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and Néel vector dynamics.
result: They find that the asymmetric effective exchange fields on the two sublattices enable deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using altermagnets in spintronic devices, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Predicting Interface And Spin States In Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Junctions
authors: Sofia Sanz And Daniel Sánchez-Portal

motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the paper focuses on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states based on width combinations and junction geometries.
result: The number of interface states depends on more than just width differences, requiring detailed modeling.
conclusion: Predicting interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is nontrivial and requires beyond-simple considerations.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in photonic systems, analogous to the spin Hall effect but for orbital angular momentum.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall-like effect for light carrying orbital angular momentum, extending the concept of the spin Hall effect to vortex beams.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic system with loss/gain gradients and derive the equations of motion for vortex light, showing that the orbital angular momentum couples to the gradient, leading to transverse deflection.
result: They demonstrate that a loss/gain gradient induces a Hall effect for vortex light, where the direction of deflection depends on the sign of the orbital angular momentum, analogous to the spin Hall effect.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling light with orbital angular momentum using non-Hermitian photonic structures, which may have applications in optical manipulation and information processing.

title: First-principles Prediction Of A Multiferroic Semiconductor With Switchable Spin-polarized Berry Curvature Dipole: ${\mathrm{PbMnO}}_{3}$:${\mathrm{PbVO}}_{3}$

conclusion: The material is a promising candidate for multifunctional devices combining ferroelectric, ferromagnetic, and topological properties.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter

tldr: This paper studies how isotopic substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing and transport properties.
motivation: Isotopic substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds it can cause more complex effects. The authors aim to understand these effects on phonon eigenvectors and transport.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to analyze parametric Hermitian perturbations due to mass changes, studying eigenvector mixing and transport in phonon manifolds.
result: They find that isotopic substitution induces collective phonon mixing and modifies eigenvector transport, with implications for thermal conductivity and vibrational dynamics.
conclusion: Isotopic substitution in solids with dense phonon manifolds leads to nontrivial modifications of phonon eigenvectors and transport, beyond simple frequency rescaling.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets

conclusion: Time delay can induce complex aging dynamics in swarmalator crystals, relevant for understanding active matter systems with non-instantaneous interactions.

title: Theory Uncertainties In Predictions Of Strong-field Qed
authors: T. G. Blackburn
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. Blackburn

Experiments using high-power lasers and relativistic electron beams will soon be capable of precision testing of the theory of strong-field quantum electrodynamics. The comparison between experiment and theory always occurs via numerical simulations, but the lack of quantitative uncertainty bounds f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023346] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses theory uncertainties in numerical simulations of strong-field QED, focusing on precision tests with high-power lasers and relativistic electron beams.
motivation: Precision tests of strong-field QED require accurate theoretical predictions, but current simulations lack quantitative uncertainty bounds.
method: The author analyzes sources of uncertainty in numerical simulations of strong-field QED processes, such as photon emission and pair production.
result: The paper identifies and quantifies dominant theory uncertainties, providing a framework for error estimation in future experiments.
conclusion: Quantifying theory uncertainties is essential for meaningful comparison between experiment and theory in strong-field QED.

title: Tiling By Near Coincidence
authors: Meshy Ochana And Ron Lifshitz
abstract:
Author(s): Meshy Ochana and Ron Lifshitz

Moiré patterns of twisted and scaled bilayers have recently emerged as a fertile source of quasiperiodic order in two-dimensional materials. Inspired by these systems, we introduce the near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane. The method is intuitive—admitting pairs …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023330] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings inspired by moiré patterns in twisted bilayers.
motivation: Moiré patterns in twisted bilayers exhibit quasiperiodic order; the authors aim to generalize this to a systematic tiling method.
method: The near-coincidence method constructs tilings by overlaying two periodic lattices with a slight mismatch in scale or rotation, then selecting vertices that are nearly coincident.
result: The method produces a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 8-fold, 10-fold, and 12-fold rotational symmetry.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method provides an intuitive and flexible framework for generating quasiperiodic tilings, with potential applications in materials science.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space framework for topological wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
