result: They demonstrate spectral flow and topological invariants in the continuous plasma system, establishing a bulk-interface correspondence.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides a robust method for studying topological phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous materials using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous systems where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix, without reference to a Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix, applicable to amorphous higher-order topological insulators.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for identifying topology in disordered systems, but is purely a condensed matter result with no quantum information or thermodynamics connection.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in a two-species random walk system.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a random walk model with diffusion, probabilistic absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex emergent behavior can occur in random walk systems with multiple species.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by quantum light, specifically bright squeezed vacuum, extending strong-field physics to nonclassical fields.
motivation: High-harmonic generation with quantum light is a new frontier, but the mechanism for nonclassical fields with vanishing mean electric field is not understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the quantum-optical Bloch equations and a generalized three-step model incorporating the quantum statistics of the driving field.
result: They show that HHG with bright squeezed vacuum exhibits unique features such as photon-number-dependent harmonic spectra and entanglement between harmonics and the driving field.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for understanding HHG with quantum light and opens possibilities for generating entangled photon pairs at high harmonics.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, and Mordechai Segev

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle time refraction at optical frequencies by modulating refractive index on ultrafast timescales.
motivation: To achieve and measure order-unity refractive index changes within an optical cycle, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
method: Experimental setup using a pump-probe scheme with a modulated medium to induce and probe subcycle refractive index variations.
result: Observation of subcycle time refraction with order-unity index changes at optical frequencies.
conclusion: Subcycle refractive index modulation is feasible and can be measured, opening possibilities for ultrafast optical control.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant for understanding axion electrodynamics in condensed matter.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The observation of surface ferromagnons provides evidence for the axion-insulating phase and highlights the role of surface magnetism in topological insulators.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escape events.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed significantly below the mode coupling temperature to analyze particle trajectories and identify cage escape events.
result: Rare cage escapes are found to dominate the relaxation process, providing new insights into the dynamics of deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The study highlights the importance of rare events in glassy dynamics and offers a microscopic picture of relaxation.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and training instabilities.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in neural networks to improve training stability and interpretability.
method: Analytical modeling of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent networks, combined with numerical simulations.
result: Identifies ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and suggests ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning, with implications for designing more stable recurrent networks.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of quantum chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental signatures.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent supersymmetry and enabling future studies of strongly coupled theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, focusing on magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2.
motivation: To understand and control spin textures in moiré superlattices for potential information manipulation.
method: Neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are revealed in EuAg4Sb2.
conclusion: Establishes a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand whether topological magnon gaps survive at finite temperatures, which is important for spintronic device applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures, likely using many-body perturbation theory or spin-wave theory.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, with implications for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational hardness of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic tools.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for designing cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The framework integrates physical constraints (e.g., conservation laws, symmetries) into a machine learning model to infer causal links from time-series data.
result: The method outperforms standard causal inference techniques on several benchmark network dynamics datasets.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal link prediction in networks, offering a new tool for analyzing complex systems.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or topological arguments.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to characterize the magnetic properties and critical exponents.
result: The system undergoes a phase transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and nonlinear susceptibility indicates hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel ground state in kagome ice systems, with implications for frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using ARPES.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures; finding room-temperature flat bands is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and performed angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for studying correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated physics and potential quantum phases at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic transitions.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and their critical behavior at the liquid-vapor transition is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical exponents and scaling behavior of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-gas critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal novel critical phenomena in hyperuniform systems, relevant to soft matter physics but not to the user's research directions.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a purely condensed matter physics result with no quantum information or thermodynamics angle.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures, measuring spin-dependent electron trajectories.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect, with gate-tunable spin coherence.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-based electron optics, but the work is focused on spintronics and condensed matter, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for extracting features from data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: This work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical applications in topological data analysis, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap for bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, using techniques from topological quantum computing and implementing it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum computer, showing that the quantum algorithm can approximate the Jones polynomial for certain inputs, and discuss the resource requirements and potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may be a viable candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage in the near term.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to express any photonic state as a linear combination of simpler states, then employ photon catalysis (adding and subtracting photons) to realize the decomposition experimentally.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a universal and efficient recipe for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics experiments.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Linear system solving is a central task in computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and variable-time amplitude amplification.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their complexity, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and input model assumptions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical interactions.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving with expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and application prospects.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity, driven by frustration and interference.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: Spin glasses are a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics has broad applications.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations.
result: Highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation in advancing the field.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with implications for many physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological signatures.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising candidates, but definitive experimental confirmation is still lacking.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The authors review recent work using maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations, demonstrating that statistical physics principles can predict neural activity.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including interactions underlying their formation and their own quantum features.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering topological field theory, spin textures, and quantum effects.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic and quantum technologies.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may enable novel functionalities, but the field is still developing.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new platforms for studying quantum physics beyond standard geometries.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: Presents an open-source Python library for optical layout and demonstrates its use for building modular optical systems for trapped-ion quantum computing.
motivation: Complex optical design in AMO experiments is not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup; a modular, code-to-CAD approach is needed.
method: Develops PyOpticL, a Python library that uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to automatically place optical elements, and creates modular baseplates for common subsystems.
result: Demonstrates a full laser system for strontium trapped ions achieving over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates.
conclusion: The modular approach enables scaling of optical systems for quantum computers and fosters open-source collaborative hardware design.

title: Classical Field Simulation Of Vortex Lattice Melting In A Two-dimensional Fast Rotating Bose Gas
authors: Sálvio J Bereta, Lucas Madeira, Mônica A Caracanhas, Hélène Perrin And Romain Dubessy
abstract: We present a classical field simulation study of the thermal melting of a two-dimensional (2D) vortex lattice in a rotating Bose gas, focusing on the role of finite-size effects on the melting temperature. This work constitutes a numerical continuation of the recent experimental investigation reported in (Sharma 2024 Phys. Rev. Lett.133 143401), which addressed the thermal melting of a vortex lattice in a quasi-2D Bose gas. Using the stochastic projected Gross–Pitaevskii equation in a harmonic plus quartic trap, we simulate the finite-temperature equilibrium state and extract vortex configurations from density snapshots. Clear signatures of the two-step Kosterlitz–Thouless–Halperin–Nelson–Young melting scenario are identified. Our simulations enable a detailed characterization of the crystalline, hexatic, and liquid phases through correlation functions quantifying the translational and orientational order and through defect statistics. Finite-size effects are shown to play a crucial role at lower rotation frequencies, affecting the proliferation of lattice defects.
tldr: Classical field simulation of vortex lattice melting in a rotating 2D Bose gas, focusing on finite-size effects and the KTHNY melting scenario.
motivation: To numerically study the thermal melting of a vortex lattice in a rotating Bose gas, complementing recent experiments and clarifying the role of finite-size effects.
method: Uses the stochastic projected Gross–Pitaevskii equation to simulate finite-temperature equilibrium states in a harmonic plus quartic trap, extracting vortex configurations from density snapshots.
result: Observes clear signatures of two-step KTHNY melting (crystalline, hexatic, liquid phases) and finds that finite-size effects significantly affect defect proliferation at lower rotation frequencies.
conclusion: Finite-size effects are crucial for accurately modeling vortex lattice melting, especially at lower rotation frequencies, and the classical field approach captures the essential physics.

title: Direct Derivation Of The Modified Langevin Noise Formalism From The Canonical Quantization Of Macroscopic Electromagnetism
authors: A Ciattoni
abstract: The modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF) models the interaction of the quantized electromagnetic field with an arbitrary lossy magneto-dielectric object placed in vacuum using three types of non-interacting bosonic polaritons: scattering, electric, and magnetic. These respectively represent free-space photons scattered by the object, and photons radiated by quantized electric and magnetic dipolar sources embedded within its volume. Recently (Ciattoni 2024 Phys. Rev. A110 013707), this formalism was justified from the canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism (CQME) (Philbin 2010 New J. Phys.12 123008) in the Heisenberg picture. This was achieved by identifying the polariton operators within the formal solution of the macroscopic Maxwell equations, assuming they obey bosonic commutation relations to retrieve the canonical ones, and showing they diagonalize the CQME Hamiltonian. However, the explicit functional dependence of these polaritons on the underlying canonical field operators remained undetermined. In this paper, we derive the exact analytical expressions for the polariton operators in terms of the canonical CQME field operators. Using these mappings, we provide a direct and rigorous derivation of the MLNF from the canonical theory in the Schrödinger picture. Our derivation is structured in three foundational steps: 1) adopting the derived analytical expressions as the constitutive definitions of the polariton operators; 2) mathematically proving that these operators are strictly bosonic as a direct consequence of the canonical commutation relations; and 3) demonstrating that they exactly diagonalize the macroscopic CQME Hamiltonian.
tldr: This paper derives explicit analytical expressions for polariton operators in the modified Langevin noise formalism from canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism.
motivation: To provide a direct and rigorous derivation of the modified Langevin noise formalism from canonical quantization, clarifying the relationship between polariton operators and canonical field operators.
method: The authors derive exact analytical mappings between polariton operators and canonical field operators, then prove bosonic commutation relations and diagonalization of the Hamiltonian.
result: Explicit functional forms for scattering, electric, and magnetic polariton operators are obtained, and their bosonic nature and Hamiltonian diagonalization are proven.
conclusion: The modified Langevin noise formalism is rigorously derived from canonical quantization, confirming its consistency and providing a solid foundation for modeling quantized electromagnetic fields in lossy media.

title: A Frequency-domain Identifiability Law For Deterministic Reconstruction Of Complex Networks Under Partial Observability
authors: Tianlong Fan And Linyuan Lü Xiaoxiao Liang
abstract: Inferring network architecture from partial behavioral observations is central to computational studies of complex systems, with implications for detecting covert actors in terrorist networks, localizing unobserved brain regions, and revealing latent molecular regulators. Focusing on evolutionary game dynamics, we uncover an empirically consistent frequency-domain regularity: the aggregated magnitude of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of a node’s payoff time series scales linearly with its structural degree, , across tested topologies and parameter regimes. Leveraging this structure–behavior scaling, we develop a deterministic inference framework that (i) estimates degrees directly from DFT spectra via a single global-slope fit, and (ii) uses brief, identifiability-oriented local interventions (‘suppress-and-measure’) to reveal adjacencies through intervention-induced spectral drops. Discrepancies between estimated degree and revealed neighbors deterministically enumerate external edges to hidden components and yield tight lower/upper bounds on the number of unobserved nodes. We analyze the conditions under which the scaling holds, quantify deviations under structural heterogeneity, and characterize sample-length dependence. Experiments on synthetic and empirical networks demonstrate accurate topology recovery, robustness to stochasticity, and scalability to thousand-node graphs, with consistent gains over causality-, correlation-, information-, and likelihood-based baselines. These results establish a DFT-based route to structure discovery under partial observability, translating local spectral measurements into actionable structural information.
tldr: This paper uses DFT of payoff time series to infer network structure from partial observations in evolutionary game dynamics.
motivation: Inferring hidden network architecture from limited behavioral data is important for detecting covert actors, unobserved brain regions, or latent molecular regulators.
method: The authors discover a linear scaling between the aggregated DFT magnitude of a node's payoff time series and its degree, then use a global-slope fit to estimate degrees and a 'suppress-and-measure' intervention to reveal adjacencies.
result: The method accurately recovers network topology on synthetic and empirical networks, outperforming causality-, correlation-, information-, and likelihood-based baselines, and provides bounds on unobserved nodes.
conclusion: The DFT-based approach offers a deterministic, scalable route to structure discovery under partial observability.

title: Strong Field Ionized Electron Trajectories Driven By Squeezed Light
authors: Alex Schimmoller And Alexandra S Landsman
abstract: In atomic strong field ionization, a photoelectron’s motion is largely determined by the laser pulse’s expected electric field, as well as the atomic potential. However, when the ionization is performed by squeezed light, the photon’s quantum statistics can modify these dynamics. In this work, we generalize the classical trajectory Monte–Carlo technique to study strong field ionization by squeezed states of light. We find that electrons driven by phase-squeezed pulses exhibit increases in longitudinal momentum consistent with what is expected from the field statistics. Meanwhile, the transverse momentum distribution shows varying influence of ‘hard’ and ‘soft’ rescattering off the Coulomb potential, and the proportion of electrons recaptured as Rydberg states decreases monotonically with the amount of squeezed light applied. This work demonstrates the added experimental control over ultrafast electron dynamics achievable by tuning light’s quantum statistics, as well as the essential role of the atomic potential in strong field ionization.
tldr: This paper studies how squeezed light affects electron trajectories in strong field ionization, using a classical trajectory Monte Carlo method.
motivation: To understand how quantum statistics of light (squeezing) can modify ultrafast electron dynamics beyond classical field expectations.
method: Generalized classical trajectory Monte Carlo technique to simulate strong field ionization by squeezed states of light.
result: Phase-squeezed pulses increase longitudinal momentum; transverse momentum shows rescattering effects; Rydberg recapture decreases with squeezing.
conclusion: Tuning quantum statistics of light offers experimental control over ultrafast electron dynamics, but atomic potential remains crucial.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye And Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals are ubiquitous in nature. They represent unique aperiodic materials featuring long-range order that occupy an intermediate niche between exactly periodic and disordered materials. These properties are reflected in the unusual evolutionary dynamics of excitations and unique localization properties of linear eigenmodes supported by quasicrystals. In particular, being the structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry of order , photonic quasicrystals can support the stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states has not been investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices are considered in this context. Here, we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects—disclinations—introduced into their structure that allows to produce novel quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from the basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches the linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We find two different classes of stable vortex solitons comprising in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting a particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, whereas stability intervals for them broaden with the decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals. Our results extend the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting emerging prospects for the robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: This paper studies vortex solitons in photonic quasicrystals with disclinations, focusing on their stability and intensity distributions.
motivation: To understand how global topological defects (disclinations) in quasicrystals affect the properties of vortex light states, which had not been investigated before.
method: The authors propose a class of quasicrystals with disclinations, analyze their linear spectrum, and numerically simulate the propagation of vortex solitons.
result: They find two classes of stable vortex solitons with in-phase or out-of-phase bright spots, and show that low-charge vortex solitons can be stable, with stability intervals broadening as rotational symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The results extend localization theory in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, offering potential for robust transmission of power or information.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on elastic and magnetic coupling.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic orders in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked under stress, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Compression-Driven Anomaly Detection In Brain Mri Using An Interpretable Quantum Autoencoder
authors: Santanu Ganguly, Xing Liang, Dimitrios Makris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quantum autoencoder (QAE) for compression-driven anomaly detection in brain MRI data. The approach leverages angle encoding to map image patches into quantum states, followed by a variational encoder-decoder architecture trained to discard information via auxiliary trash qubits. Anomaly scores reflect the degree to which inputs resist compression relative to normal data, with higher scores corresponding to deviations from the learned normal manifold. Evaluated on publicly available brain MRI DICOM datasets, the method achieves a slice-level ROC-AUC of approximately 0.95 and a patch-level ROC-AUC of approximately 0.813, outperforming classical autoencoder and PCA baselines. Analysis of the learned parameters reveals a pronounced encoder-decoder asymmetry, where effective anomaly detection arises from structured information compression within the encoder rather than increased parameter magnitude or decoder expressivity. This results in a controlled compression-reconstruction trade-off with a clear operating regime that supports principled threshold selection. Qualitative evaluation further shows that the QAE produces spatially localized anomaly heatmaps aligned with tumorous regions. The results, supported by promising baseline performances, demonstrate that quantum autoencoders provide an interpretable and controllable mechanism for anomaly detection based on incompressibility with respect to a learned latent representation. This work highlights the potential of quantum autoencoders as a principled tool for studying compression dynamics in quantum machine learning, with promising implications for decision support in medical imaging workflows.
tldr: A quantum autoencoder is applied to anomaly detection in brain MRI, achieving high ROC-AUC scores.
motivation: To leverage quantum machine learning for interpretable and controllable anomaly detection in medical imaging.
method: Angle encoding maps image patches to quantum states; a variational encoder-decoder with trash qubits learns to compress normal data; anomaly scores measure reconstruction error.
result: Slice-level ROC-AUC of 0.95 and patch-level ROC-AUC of 0.813, outperforming classical baselines; encoder-decoder asymmetry is observed.
conclusion: Quantum autoencoders offer a principled, interpretable approach to anomaly detection based on incompressibility, with potential for medical decision support.

title: Vector Representation Of Exact Soliton Dynamics In Multi-component Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Systems
authors: Maxime Foucher, Laurent Delisle, Amine Jaouadi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multicomponent nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations constitute fundamental models for coherent matter waves in multicomponent Bose--Einstein condensates, spinor quantum fluids, and vector nonlinear optical systems. We develop a vector formulation of the Hirota bilinear formalism for the completely integrable Manakov system that treats the coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations directly at the vector level rather than through the conventional component-wise decomposition. This framework naturally retains the intrinsic multicomponent representation of the model while providing compact analytical expressions for exact vector soliton solutions. Within this approach, we systematically construct bright, dark, and mixed one-, two-, and three-soliton solutions and show how the underlying vector structure provides a unified description of their nonlinear interactions. In particular, the proposed formalism makes the coupling between the different components explicit while preserving the geometric organization of the vector system throughout the bilinearization procedure. Beyond its analytical simplicity, the framework offers a natural perspective for the study of coherent multicomponent nonlinear excitations and provides a foundation for extending vector Hirota methods to other classes of exact solutions, including rogue waves, periodic waves, and rational solutions.
tldr: This paper develops a vector formulation of the Hirota bilinear method for the Manakov system to obtain exact soliton solutions.
motivation: To provide a compact, vector-level description of soliton dynamics in multicomponent nonlinear Schrödinger systems, avoiding component-wise decomposition.
method: Extends the Hirota bilinear formalism to the vector level, treating coupled equations directly and constructing bright, dark, and mixed soliton solutions.
result: Obtains analytical expressions for one-, two-, and three-soliton solutions, showing explicit coupling between components and a unified description of interactions.
conclusion: The vector Hirota method offers a natural framework for multicomponent nonlinear excitations and can be extended to other exact solutions like rogue waves.

title: Enhancing Co-packaging Optics Enabled Silicon Photonics Security Assurance Hardware Fingerprinting
authors: Liton Kumar Biswas, M Shafkat M Khan, Himanandhan Reddy Kottur, Hao Wang, Hamed Dalir, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon photonics enables integration of optical components using standard semiconductor processes, greatly improving data communication bandwidth and energy efficiency. However, photonics integrated circuits (PICs) face unique security challenges, such as counterfeit or tampering threats, that conventional electronic security methods do not address. We propose a novel hardware fingerprinting technique that embeds two dimensional photonic crystal patterns into the density control filler regions of a PIC. Each PhC pattern is designed to resonate a specific visible to near infrared wavelengths, producing a distinctive optical signature (based on wavelength, polarization, and incident angle) for each device. Finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation using ANSYS Lumerical is employed to optimize nanostructure dimensions and spacing so that each device's reflection/absorption spectrum contains unique narrowband peaks. No extra fabrication steps or materials are required beyond standard lithography, keeping costs low. The embedded nanostructures have sub-50nm precision, making forgery extremely difficult. Our method yields a high resolution, scalable fingerprint for silicon photonic chips, enabling cost-effective device authentication and improved supply chain security.
tldr: A hardware fingerprinting technique for silicon photonic chips using embedded photonic crystal patterns for authentication.
motivation: Silicon photonics integrated circuits face unique security threats like counterfeiting and tampering that electronic methods cannot address.
method: Embed two-dimensional photonic crystal patterns into density control filler regions of PICs; each pattern produces a unique optical signature based on wavelength, polarization, and incident angle, optimized via FDTD simulations.
result: The method yields high-resolution, scalable fingerprints with sub-50nm precision, requiring no extra fabrication steps.
conclusion: This approach enables cost-effective device authentication and improved supply chain security for silicon photonic chips.

title: Parameter-Efficient Quantum-Inspired Fast Weight Programmers For Traffic-Matrix Forecasting
authors: Kuo-Chung Peng, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chun-Hua Lin, Tai-Yue Li, Nan-Yow Chen, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic matrices (TMs) capture network-wide origin-destination demand and are central to traffic engineering, yet accurate whole-matrix forecasting remains challenging when prediction must be performed under the memory, update, and training-budget constraints of online network control. This paper investigates whether compact quantum-inspired recurrent models can provide effective TM forecasts without relying on dedicated graph, transformer, or diffusion modules. We adapt gated quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold network fast-weight programmers (QKAN-FWPs) to direct multi-step Abilene TM forecasting, where each model predicts the next 20 five-minute frames of a 144-channel origin-destination (OD) matrix from a two-hour history. We benchmark three QKAN placement variants against a matched-size long short-term memory (LSTM) network, a larger LSTM, and a classical gated fast-weight programmer under a shared fixed-budget training protocol. Among the evaluated recurrent models, G-QKANFWP achieves the best pooled root-mean-square error (RMSE), while using only 22.4% of the larger LSTM. It also outperforms both the matched-size LSTM and the classical G-FWP baseline, indicating that the gain is not due to gated fast-weight framework alone. Convergence and channel-wise analyses further show that the quantum-inspired variants obtain lower validation-loss area under the learning curve (AULC) than matched-size recurrent baselines, while G-QKANFWP and GQKAN-FWP achieve substantially more OD-channel wins. These results identify a classical slow programmer with a quantum-inspired fast programmer as a promising accuracy-efficiency design for resource-conscious network traffic-matrix forecasting.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-inspired recurrent models to traffic matrix forecasting, achieving accuracy gains with fewer parameters.
motivation: Accurate traffic matrix forecasting under memory and training constraints is challenging; compact models are needed for online network control.
method: The authors adapt gated quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold network fast-weight programmers (QKAN-FWPs) to predict multi-step Abilene traffic matrices, comparing variants against LSTM and classical fast-weight programmer baselines.
result: The G-QKANFWP variant achieves the best RMSE using only 22.4% of the larger LSTM's parameters and outperforms matched-size baselines.
conclusion: Quantum-inspired fast weight programmers offer a promising accuracy-efficiency trade-off for resource-constrained traffic forecasting.

title: Nonextensive Statistical Signatures Of The Bilaterian Transition In Proteome Length Distributions
authors: Sertac Eroglu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protein length distributions across the tree of life carry a quantitative signature of organismal complexity. Nonextensive statistical mechanics, through the Tsallis generalized entropy formalism, provides a natural framework for describing complex systems characterized by long-range correlations, scale invariance, and hierarchical organization -- features that classical Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics cannot accommodate. In this work, the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) of protein lengths is analyzed within this framework for the reference proteomes of 22 fully sequenced organisms spanning the domains Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya, with deliberate sampling across the animal transition zone from sponges and cnidarians to higher bilaterians. Maximum likelihood (MLE) fitting of truncated discrete q-exponential distributions, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reveals that the entropic index q resolves into three statistically distinct regimes: superextensive (q < 1) for prokaryotes, unicellular and non-animal multicellular eukaryotes, and basal animals; a boundary regime (CI on spanning unity) for the two cnidarians studied and the basal bilaterian C. teleta; and subextensive (q > 1) for all higher bilaterians, with q increasing monotonically across the four deuterostomes sampled from S. purpuratus (1.033) to H. sapiens (1.147). The q-exponential outperforms the ordinary exponential distribution across all 22 proteomes and becomes progressively more competitive against alternative two-parameter distributions as proteome complexity increases. These results identify the Tsallis entropic index as a continuous, physically interpretable indicator of proteome organizational complexity and extend the applicability of nonextensive statistical mechanics to proteomic systems.
tldr: This paper applies nonextensive statistical mechanics to analyze protein length distributions across species, identifying the Tsallis entropic index as a marker of organismal complexity.
motivation: To find a quantitative signature of organismal complexity in proteome length distributions that classical Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics cannot capture.
method: Maximum likelihood fitting of truncated discrete q-exponential distributions to complementary cumulative distribution functions of protein lengths from 22 reference proteomes, with bootstrap confidence intervals.
result: The entropic index q resolves into three regimes: superextensive (q<1) for prokaryotes and basal animals, boundary (q≈1) for cnidarians and a basal bilaterian, and subextensive (q>1) for higher bilaterians, increasing monotonically with complexity.
conclusion: The Tsallis entropic index provides a continuous, physically interpretable indicator of proteome organizational complexity, extending nonextensive statistical mechanics to proteomics.

title: Constructions And Characterizations Of $s$-Plateaued Partitions
authors: Jiaxin Wang, Yadi Wei, Fang-Wei Fu, Jin Li, Fulin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in constructing bent functions and have rich connections with coding theory and combinatorics. In this paper, we introduce [MATH]-plateaued partitions, which generalize the bent partitions. Let [MATH] be a partition of [MATH], where [MATH] is an [MATH]-dimensional vector space over the prime field [MATH] and [MATH]. Then [MATH] is called an [MATH]-plateaued partition of [MATH] of depth [MATH] if each [MATH]-ary function [MATH] for which every [MATH] has exactly [MATH] of sets [MATH] in [MATH] in its preimage set, is a [MATH]-ary [MATH]-plateaued function. By using an [MATH]-plateaued partition, a large number of [MATH]-ary [MATH]-plateaued functions, vectorial [MATH]-plateaued functions and generalized [MATH]-plateaued functions can be constructed. In particular, [MATH]-plateaued partitions are just bent partitions. In general, [MATH]-plateaued partitions are much more complicated than bent partitions. We analyze the possible cardinality of [MATH] of an [MATH]-plateaued partition. We give some explicit constructions of [MATH]-plateaued partitions for which any generated [MATH]-ary [MATH]-plateaued function has no nonzero linear structure. We give a characterization of an [MATH]-plateaued partition [MATH], where [MATH] is odd, [MATH] and [MATH]. Based on which, we show that if [MATH], then the preimage set partition of a [MATH]-ary [MATH]-plateaued function [MATH] with [MATH] is an [MATH]-plateaued partition if and only if [MATH] is of [MATH]-form, where [MATH] is even.When [MATH], we partially address an open problem on whether a bent partition [MATH] of [MATH] of depth [MATH] must be obtained from spreads.
tldr: This paper introduces s-plateaued partitions, a generalization of bent partitions, and studies their constructions and characterizations over finite fields.
motivation: Bent partitions are important for constructing bent functions and have connections to coding theory and combinatorics; this work extends the concept to s-plateaued partitions to enable construction of plateaued functions.
