method: A lightweight meta-learner predicts image-specific priors for a sequential E-process, enabling anytime-valid certification that adaptively allocates compute resources.
result: The method achieves a 20-fold reduction in sample complexity compared to traditional RS while maintaining rigorous statistical guarantees and similar certification performance.
conclusion: The approach enables real-time, safety-critical certification deployments by allowing adaptive resource allocation based on application-specific risk thresholds.

title: Room For Error: Large-Scale Simulation Of Over-the-Air Acoustic Attacks
authors: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While voice control is rapidly becoming a ubiquitous vector of human-AI communication, the risks facing these systems remain poorly understood. This is, in part, a product of the difficulties in scaling strictly digital adversarial workflows to the physical world. These scale barriers have led the community to abstract away key acoustic factors relating to detectability and the influence of geometry on acoustics. These methodological and metrological shortcomings undermine our understanding of risk. We illuminate these issues through real-world testing, conceptual discussions, and a novel, high-throughput reality simulation framework. By testing over 8 million adversarial evaluations, we demonstrate that acoustic awareness yields relative Word Error Rate increases of up to 94.5\% under Whisper and wav2vec. We employ this framework to explore a formalize and operationalize a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio to decouple source stealth from victim attack efficacy, resolving a crucial limitation in current works. This lays the groundwork for repeatable, verifiable research that embraces, rather than abstracts, the acoustic environment.
tldr: This paper studies acoustic adversarial attacks on voice control systems, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Voice control systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, but scaling digital attacks to the physical world is difficult due to acoustic factors.
method: The authors develop a high-throughput simulation framework that models acoustic propagation and detectability, testing over 8 million adversarial evaluations.
result: Acoustic-aware attacks achieve up to 94.5% relative Word Error Rate increase on Whisper and wav2vec models.
conclusion: The work formalizes a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio to separate source stealth from attack efficacy, enabling repeatable acoustic adversarial research.

title: Beating Trivial Time For Tricky Triangle Tasks
authors: Ryan Williams Neha Pant
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For several well-studied triangle detection problems in the literature, the trivial enumeration algorithms are known to be optimal (up to the exponent) assuming popular fine-grained conjectures. For example, All-Edges Sparse Triangle and Sparse Monochromatic Triangle where each node has degree [MATH] for some [MATH], and the Exact Triangle where edges have arbitrary weights, all have this property under the 3SUM Conjecture. However, as there are slightly nontrivial algorithms for 3SUM, it is natural to wonder if the trivial algorithm for these tricky triangle tasks might also be improved. Applying a variety of techniques from randomized algorithms, circuit complexity, and communication complexity, we present the first improvements over the trivial algorithms for each of these problems in the Word RAM model. Moreover, our algorithms can be implemented with only polysize [MATH] operations on words. Extending our techniques, we also show how to solve the notorious 4-cycle detection problem on [MATH]-node graphs in [MATH] time, in a Word-RAM model with word size [MATH]. Along the way, we show how to sort [MATH] items over a universe of size [MATH] using only [MATH] word operations in [MATH] time.
tldr: This paper presents improved algorithms for triangle detection and 4-cycle detection problems in the Word RAM model, using techniques from randomized algorithms, circuit complexity, and communication complexity.
motivation: The trivial enumeration algorithms for certain triangle detection problems are believed to be optimal under fine-grained conjectures, but the authors aim to find nontrivial improvements.
method: The authors apply a variety of techniques including randomized algorithms, circuit complexity, and communication complexity to design new algorithms in the Word RAM model.
result: They present the first improvements over trivial algorithms for All-Edges Sparse Triangle, Sparse Monochromatic Triangle, and Exact Triangle, and also solve 4-cycle detection in subquadratic time.
conclusion: The results show that nontrivial improvements are possible for these problems, challenging the optimality of trivial algorithms under standard conjectures.

title: ToE: A Hierarchical And Explainable Claim Verification Framework With Dynamic Multi-source Evidence Retrieval And Aggregation
authors: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Kun Zheng, Zhen Li, Xin Li, Chunlei Li, Jiamou Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid spread of fake news poses increasing threats to information ecosystems, especially as AI-generated misinformation under Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) poisoning allows adversarially crafted content to be systematically surfaced by retrieval systems, contaminating LLM reasoning. In this paper, we propose Tree of Evidence (ToE), a hierarchical evidence reasoning framework for automated fact-checking that models each claim as a dynamically expanding argument tree. ToE integrates a reinforcement learning-driven multi-source retrieval agent, an evidence evaluation agent, and an argument tree aggregation algorithm to iteratively decompose, retrieve, and verify claims through an explainable evidence chain. We further provide a theoretical analysis of the retrieval process, deriving a formal error bound that guarantees the learned policy converges to a neighborhood of the information-theoretically optimal policy. Experiments across multiple datasets and backbone LLMs demonstrate that ToE achieves improvements ranging from 4 to 24 percentage points over competitive baselines, with particularly pronounced gains on adversarially poisoned inputs.
tldr: A hierarchical evidence reasoning framework for automated fact-checking using reinforcement learning and multi-source retrieval.
motivation: Fake news and AI-generated misinformation threaten information ecosystems; existing fact-checking methods lack explainability and robustness against adversarial content.
method: Proposes Tree of Evidence (ToE), which dynamically expands claims into argument trees, uses a reinforcement learning-driven retrieval agent, an evidence evaluation agent, and an aggregation algorithm to iteratively verify claims.
result: Achieves 4–24 percentage point improvements over baselines across datasets, with strong gains on adversarially poisoned inputs.
conclusion: ToE provides an explainable and effective approach to automated fact-checking, with theoretical guarantees on retrieval policy convergence.

title: Triadic Werewolf: A Jester Role For Multi-Hop Theory Of Mind In LLMs
authors: Avni Mittal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Theory-of-mind evaluations of large language models typically use dyadic social-deduction games, where every observable cue points to a single hidden side, so a model with strong language priors can score well without ever simulating opponents' incentives. We extend the Werewolf game with a Jester, a third faction whose utility on peer suspicion is inverted because it wins by being voted out, so optimal play requires reasoning across three opposing utility functions. Across 60 games on GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B with Jester self-learning on and off, the Jester wins 60-70% of games while Werewolves never exceed 20%, and GPT-4.1 wolves vote the Jester out on day 1 in 60-70% of games, a strictly self-defeating action. Self-learning helps DeepSeek and Llama but hurts GPT-4.1, with the cost landing on Villagers rather than Werewolves. Only DeepSeek learns the subtle strategy of looking suspicious without looking intentionally suspicious, and it gains the most from the loop. Triadic incentive structure exposes a layer of multi-agent reasoning that dyadic deduction games leave invisible.
tldr: This paper introduces a triadic Werewolf game variant with a Jester role to evaluate multi-hop theory of mind in LLMs.
motivation: Standard dyadic social-deduction games may not fully test LLMs' ability to reason about multiple opposing incentives.
method: The authors extend the Werewolf game with a Jester faction that wins by being voted out, and run 60 games on GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B with and without self-learning.
result: The Jester wins 60-70% of games; GPT-4.1 wolves often vote out the Jester on day 1, a self-defeating action; self-learning helps DeepSeek and Llama but hurts GPT-4.1.
conclusion: Triadic incentive structures reveal multi-agent reasoning capabilities that dyadic games miss, and self-learning can have asymmetric effects.

title: Ramses: Secure High-performance Computing For Sensitive Data
authors: Peter Heger, Lech Nieroda, Roland Pabel, Christoph Stollwerk, Stefan Borowski, Kamil Tokmakov, Michael Commer, Martin Peifer, Stefan Wesner, Viktor Achter
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditionally, the architecture of high-performance computing (HPC) systems is tailored for speed, while highly secure computer systems must sacrifice speed for security. However, a wide range of scientific domains, such as the life sciences, call for a combination of performance and security to allow processing sensitive data at scale. Here, we present RAMSES (Research Accelerator for Modeling and Simulation with Enhanced Security), an HPC system designed from the ground up to deliver high performance within a robust security framework. RAMSES integrates hardware-based memory encryption of AMD processors with state-of-the-art file encryption from IBM Storage Scale and the Thales CipherTrust manager, establishing an HPC platform that ensures continuous encryption throughout the data life cycle - at rest, in transit, and in use - in compliance with major data protection standards (European General Data Protection Regulation, ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and Federal Information Processing Standards). In addition, we implemented advanced operating system hardening, a multi-layered security architecture, and mandatory multi-factor authentication to adapt the HPC environment to increased security demands. Benchmark results from the biomedical sector demonstrate that the performance impact of the secure environment is limited and that integration of the conflicting requirements speed and security can be achieved while preserving a coherent, flexible, and user-friendly system.
tldr: This paper presents RAMSES, an HPC system designed for secure processing of sensitive data, with a focus on encryption and compliance.
motivation: Scientific domains like life sciences require both high performance and robust security for processing sensitive data at scale.
method: The system integrates hardware-based memory encryption, file encryption, OS hardening, multi-factor authentication, and a multi-layered security architecture.
result: Benchmark results from the biomedical sector show limited performance impact from the security measures.
conclusion: It is possible to achieve both high performance and strong security in an HPC system while maintaining usability.

title: How Humans, Bots, And Agents Communicate About Vulnerabilities In Pull Requests
authors: Pien Rooijendijk, Christoph Treude, Mairieli Wessel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Developers may reference vulnerabilities in pull request discussions through both explicit identifiers, such as CVEs or GHSAs, and implicit security-related language (e.g., "unauthorized access" or "SQL injection"). Prior work has primarily focused on explicit identifiers, potentially overlooking vulnerability discussions that lack formal references. Bots and coding agents are becoming more common in pull requests, raising new questions about how different accounts communicate about vulnerabilities. In this registered report, we describe our planned study of vulnerability communication in pull requests by humans, bots, and coding agents. Building on the AIDev-pop dataset, we analyze explicit vulnerability references and implicit security-related signals across pull request titles, descriptions, review comments, commit messages, and timeline discussions. We further investigate whether these references are associated with vulnerabilities introduced or fixed in the modified code and how they relate to pull request review activity and outcomes. This study contributes a large-scale empirical investigation of vulnerability communication practices in modern software development.
tldr: This paper studies how humans, bots, and coding agents communicate about vulnerabilities in pull request discussions, focusing on explicit and implicit security references.
motivation: Prior work has overlooked implicit security language and the role of bots/agents in vulnerability communication.
method: The authors plan to analyze the AIDev-pop dataset, examining explicit vulnerability identifiers and implicit security signals across various pull request components.
result: The paper is a registered report describing a planned study; no results are presented yet.
conclusion: The study aims to provide a large-scale empirical investigation of vulnerability communication practices in modern software development.

abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the relationship between tree species richness and watershed multifunctionality, finding a positive but climate-dependent effect.
motivation: Understanding how biodiversity shapes ecosystem functions across large landscapes is crucial for conservation and management.
method: The authors analyzed forest tree diversity and watershed multifunctionality data across a large geographic scale, using statistical models to assess the effect of species richness and its interaction with aridity.
result: Higher tree species richness increases watershed multifunctionality, but the effect weakens in arid climates.
conclusion: Biodiversity conservation is important for maintaining ecosystem multifunctionality, especially in less arid regions.

title: Transient Large-Scale Anisotropy In TeV Cosmic Rays Due To An Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection
authors: Zhen Cao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Cao et al. (LHAASO Collaboration)

A solar storm hitting Earth appears to have reduced the amount of incoming high-energy cosmic rays, suggesting a new way of measuring solar activity.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251002] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a transient large-scale anisotropy in TeV cosmic rays caused by an interplanetary coronal mass ejection, observed by the LHAASO collaboration.
motivation: To understand the modulation of high-energy cosmic rays by solar activity and to develop new methods for measuring solar storms.
method: Analysis of data from the LHAASO observatory, measuring the flux and anisotropy of TeV cosmic rays during a solar storm event.
result: A significant reduction and anisotropic distribution of cosmic rays were observed, correlated with the passage of a coronal mass ejection.
conclusion: Solar storms can be detected and characterized through their effect on cosmic ray anisotropy, offering a new tool for space weather monitoring.

title: Pattern Formation During Melting Of Lamellar Eutectics
authors: Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, And Silvère Akamatsu
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, and Silvère Akamatsu

A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting of a two-phase eutectic solid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256301] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pattern formation during melting of lamellar eutectics, a topic in materials science and solidification physics.
motivation: Understanding pattern formation in eutectic melting is important for controlling microstructure in materials processing.
method: Experimental observation and theoretical modeling of melting dynamics in two-phase eutectic solids.
result: A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting, which are characterized and analyzed.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the dynamics of phase transformations in eutectic systems.

title: Synthetic Spatiotemporal Plasmonic Vortices On Chip
authors: Qian Chen, Shuoshuo Zhang, Guoyu Xian, Haoqiang Hu, Xiaohua Wu, Xiaofei Wu, Jer-Shing Huang, Chen-Bin Huang, Jin-Hui Zhong, Yuquan Zhang, Xiaocong Yuan, Changjun Min, And Yanan Dai

Spatiotemporal vortices are polychromatic modes that intertwine orbital angular momentum in space and time. Here, we introduce a new class of such vortices, “spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices,” carrying nontrivial topological spin textures. They are generated by chronotopic interference of temporall…

tldr: This paper introduces synthetic spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices on a chip, which are polychromatic modes carrying topological spin textures generated by chronotopic interference of temporally nonidentical pulses.
motivation: To create a new class of spatiotemporal vortices in plasmonic systems, enabling nontrivial topological spin textures and potential applications in nanophotonics.
method: The authors use chronotopic interference of temporally nonidentical pulses to generate spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices on a chip, characterized by their topological spin textures.
result: They demonstrate the generation and characterization of synthetic spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices with controlled topological properties.
conclusion: This work expands the concept of spatiotemporal vortices to plasmonic platforms, offering new opportunities for manipulating light-matter interactions at the nanoscale.

title: Search For Dark Matter Induced Airglow In Planetary Atmospheres
authors: Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, And Joshua Tong
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, and Joshua Tong

We point out that dark matter (DM) can illuminate planetary skies via ultraviolet airglow. Dark matter annihilation products can excite molecular hydrogen, which then deexcites to produce ultraviolet emission in the Lyman and Werner bands. We search for this new effect by analyzing nightside ultravi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251001] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper searches for dark matter induced ultraviolet airglow in planetary atmospheres as a new detection method.
motivation: Dark matter annihilation products may excite molecular hydrogen in planetary atmospheres, producing detectable UV emission.
method: The authors analyze nightside ultraviolet observations of planetary atmospheres to search for excess emission from dark matter annihilation.
result: No significant dark matter signal is found, and constraints are placed on dark matter annihilation cross-sections.
conclusion: Planetary atmospheres can serve as novel detectors for dark matter, but current data show no evidence.

title: Short Strings In Three-Dimensional Anti–de Sitter Space: From Weak To Strong Coupling
authors: Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., And Charles Thull
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., and Charles Thull

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251603] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum spectral curve for strings in AdS3 with Ramond-Ramond charge, studying the spectrum from weak to strong coupling.
motivation: To understand the spectrum of short strings in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space across coupling regimes, which is a problem in string theory and AdS/CFT.
method: Numerical solution of the conjectured quantum spectral curve, an integrability-based method.
result: At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a non-perturbative check of the AdS/CFT correspondence and the quantum spectral curve approach.

motivation: Understanding how cells form freestanding protrusions without extracellular support is important for cell biology, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

result: They find that membrane curvature can trigger instability in the gel growth, leading to pattern formation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into cytoskeletal mechanics but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Black Hole Mergers Beyond General Relativity: A Self-Force Approach
authors: Ayush Roy, Lorenzo Küchler, Adam Pound, And Rodrigo Panosso Macedo
abstract:
Author(s): Ayush Roy, Lorenzo Küchler, Adam Pound, and Rodrigo Panosso Macedo

A modular framework within the self-force formalism that applies to a large class of effective field theories of gravity in order to perform tests of general relativity with binary black hole mergers is critical for tests of general relativity that make use of the upcoming space-based gravitational wave detectors such as LISA.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251404] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a self-force formalism for testing general relativity with black hole mergers, focusing on gravitational wave astrophysics.
motivation: To enable tests of general relativity using upcoming gravitational wave detectors like LISA by modeling deviations from GR in binary black hole mergers.
method: The authors propose a modular framework within the self-force formalism that applies to a broad class of effective field theories of gravity.
result: The framework allows for systematic computation of gravitational waveforms beyond general relativity, incorporating self-force corrections.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical tool for future gravitational wave observations to constrain modifications to general relativity.

In this Letter, we present a new spectroscopy technique for detect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253802] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel chiroptical spectroscopy technique for detecting chirality via extinction differences.
motivation: Chirality detection is important in chemistry and biology; existing circular dichroism spectroscopy has limitations.
method: The authors propose a new spectroscopy technique that measures the extinction difference for circular polarizations.
result: The technique is demonstrated theoretically or experimentally (details not fully available from abstract).
conclusion: The new method offers an alternative approach to chirality detection.

title: Relating Rates Of Global Change, Evolutionary Adaptation, And Extinction
authors: Daniel H. Rothman And Sergei Petrovskii
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel H. Rothman and Sergei Petrovskii

It is widely assumed that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces a species’ capacity to adapt. However, this hypothesis lacks support at the scale of global change, in part because the distribution of adaptation rates is unknown. Here, we test this idea by formulating a general model t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the relationship between global environmental change rates, evolutionary adaptation, and extinction risk using a general mathematical framework.
motivation: To test the hypothesis that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces a species' adaptive capacity, which lacks support at the global scale due to unknown adaptation rate distributions.
method: Formulates a general model linking rates of global change, evolutionary adaptation, and extinction, likely using differential equations or stochastic processes.
result: The model provides a quantitative relationship between change rates and extinction probability, potentially identifying critical thresholds.
conclusion: The findings support the idea that extinction risk increases when environmental change exceeds adaptive capacity, offering insights for conservation under global change.

title: How The Oblique Drift Instability Alters Solar Wind Heating And Constrains The Distribution Of Solar Wind Observations

tldr: This paper studies the oblique drift instability in solar wind plasma and its effect on heating and observational constraints.
motivation: To understand how ion-driven plasma instabilities constrain solar wind observations and contribute to plasma heating.
method: The authors use linear theory and possibly simulations to analyze instability thresholds and compare with observational data.
result: The oblique drift instability alters solar wind heating and sets boundaries on stable plasma parameters.
conclusion: The instability plays a key role in regulating solar wind plasma conditions and must be accounted for in models.

title: Flexible Gravitational-Wave Parameter Estimation With Transformers
authors: Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, And Bernhard Schölkopf

Gravitational-wave data analysis relies on accurate and efficient methods to extract physical information from noisy detector signals, yet the increasing rate and complexity of observations represent a growing challenge. Deep learning provides a powerful alternative to traditional inference, but exi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies transformer neural networks to gravitational-wave parameter estimation, a topic in astrophysics and deep learning.
motivation: Gravitational-wave data analysis requires accurate and efficient parameter estimation from noisy signals, and traditional methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors develop a transformer-based deep learning model to perform flexible and fast Bayesian inference of gravitational-wave source parameters.
result: The transformer model achieves competitive accuracy and significantly faster inference compared to standard techniques like Markov chain Monte Carlo.
conclusion: Deep learning, specifically transformers, offers a promising approach for real-time gravitational-wave parameter estimation, enabling analysis of increasing observation rates.

authors: M. Ablikim et Al.

tldr: This paper tests CP symmetry in neutral decays of Λ hyperons using J/ψ→ΛΛ̄ events from BESIII.
motivation: CP violation is a key phenomenon in particle physics, and testing it in hyperon decays provides a sensitive probe of the Standard Model and potential new physics.
method: A full angular analysis of the decay J/ψ→ΛΛ̄ is performed using 10 billion J/ψ events collected by the BESIII detector, extracting decay parameters for Λ and Λ̄.
result: The decay parameters are measured with high precision, and CP symmetry is tested by comparing the parameters for Λ and Λ̄.
conclusion: The results are consistent with CP conservation within uncertainties, placing constraints on CP-violating effects in hyperon decays.

title: Probing Strong-field Ionization Dynamics In Elliptical Fields Using Two-color Phase-of-the-phase Spectroscopy

We theoretically study strong-field ionization dynamics under a two-color laser field composed of a strong 800-nm circularly polarized field and a weak 400-nm linearly polarized field. By numerically solving the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation, we obtain the photoelectron momen…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies strong-field ionization dynamics in elliptical laser fields using two-color phase-of-the-phase spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand and control strong-field ionization processes in complex laser fields, which is important for attosecond science and laser-matter interactions.
method: Numerically solves the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation for a model atom in a two-color laser field (800 nm circular + 400 nm linear) and analyzes photoelectron momentum distributions.
result: Reveals the phase-of-the-phase structure in photoelectron momentum distributions, providing insights into the ionization dynamics in elliptical fields.
conclusion: The two-color phase-of-the-phase spectroscopy is a powerful tool for probing strong-field ionization dynamics in elliptical laser fields.

title: Parity Nonconservation In Hydrogen Induced By Low-mass Vector-boson Exchange
authors: V. A. Dzuba, V. V. Flambaum, And G. K. Vong

If a hypothetical additional [MATH] boson is light, however, its contribution does not exhibit the same strong enhancement with [MATH]. As a resul…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062817] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parity nonconservation in hydrogen due to hypothetical light vector bosons, which is a topic in atomic physics and beyond-standard-model particle physics.
motivation: To investigate whether low-mass vector bosons can induce observable parity-violating effects in hydrogen, which could serve as a probe for new physics.
method: The authors calculate parity-nonconserving amplitudes in hydrogen using atomic theory and consider the exchange of a hypothetical light Z' boson between electrons and the nucleus.
result: They find that the contribution from a light boson does not scale strongly with nuclear charge Z, unlike the standard Z-boson exchange, making hydrogen a promising system for detection.
conclusion: Hydrogen atoms can be used to search for light vector bosons via parity violation measurements, complementing searches in heavier atoms.

title: Differential Momentum Measurement Of Strong-field Double Ionization Of Mg Atoms
authors: Libin Zheng, Linna Zhang, Huipeng Kang, And Xiaojun Liu

The experimental result provides direct evidence for the intermediate pathway of double ionization.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061101] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an experimental study of strong-field double ionization of Mg atoms using a time-of-flight spectrometer.
motivation: To investigate the intermediate pathway of nonsequential double ionization in strong laser fields.
method: A time-of-flight spectrometer combining laser ablation with supersonic molecular beam technique was developed to measure differential momentum of ions.
result: The experimental results provide direct evidence for the intermediate pathway of double ionization.
conclusion: The technique enables detailed momentum-resolved studies of strong-field double ionization.

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063527] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-order harmonic generation in MgO crystals using combined laser pulses, focusing on interband transition pathways.
motivation: To understand and control high-order harmonic generation in solids for potential applications in attosecond science and strong-field physics.
method: Uses a multiband strong-field approximation model to analyze pathway-resolved harmonic generation in MgO under monochromatic and combined laser pulses.
result: Identifies that combined pulses can selectively enhance or suppress specific interband transition pathways, affecting the harmonic spectrum.
conclusion: Pathway control via combined pulses offers a way to manipulate high-order harmonics in solids, relevant for ultrafast optics.

motivation: Understanding the link between structural heterogeneity and crystallization in phase-change materials is important for optimizing their performance in memory devices.
method: The authors systematically characterize spatial heterogeneity using experimental techniques and correlate it with crystallization behavior.
result: They find a clear correlation between nanoscale heterogeneity and the onset of primary crystallization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of structural disorder in crystallization, which may guide material design.

method: Crystal structure prediction combined with first-principles density functional theory calculations.
result: The Li-Xe system exhibits diverse structures and electride character under pressure.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding high-pressure chemistry of noble gas compounds.

motivation: To enhance wave energy density for improving efficiency of wave energy converters.
method: The space transformation method maps a parabolic boundary to a straight one, enabling parabolic focusing with a straight reflector.
result: Numerical simulations demonstrate effective parabolic focusing of water waves using the designed straight reflector.

motivation: To understand how suprathermal high-energy particles affect hydrodynamic instabilities in high-energy-density plasmas.
method: A single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model is developed and simulated.
result: The model describes turbulent kinetic energy evolution under the influence of high-energy particles.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for turbulence in plasmas with high-energy particles, relevant to astrophysical and fusion contexts.

title: Predicting Instantaneous Friction From Friction Damping Coefficients In Underdamped Sliding

motivation: Friction accounts for nearly one-third of global energy consumption, and the coefficient of friction's velocity dependence limits its predictive power for instantaneous friction forces.
method: The authors derive a relationship between friction damping coefficients and instantaneous friction, likely using experimental or theoretical modeling of underdamped sliding dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that friction damping coefficients can be used to predict instantaneous friction more accurately than the traditional coefficient of friction.
conclusion: The proposed approach improves prediction of friction-induced energy dissipation, which could aid in designing more efficient mechanical systems.

authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic population dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in structured populations.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of disease spread on assortative networks and analyze the probability of extinction under temporary reductions in transmission rates.
result: They find that assortative mixing can significantly alter the effectiveness of lockdowns, with optimal timing and duration depending on network structure.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns can be effective in reducing extinction risk, but their success is highly sensitive to the network's assortativity and the timing of interventions.

title: Dynamic Stabilization Of The Isolated Internal Defect In The Presence Of A Temporally Modulated Laser Prepulse
authors: Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, And W. Y. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, and W. Y. Zhang

Hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by isolated internal defects remain a critical performance-limiting factor in inertial confinement fusion experiments. Here we extend the concept of dynamic stabilization via temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive [K. G. Zhao et al.,
tldr: This paper studies dynamic stabilization of hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by internal defects in inertial confinement fusion using temporally modulated laser prepulses.
motivation: Hydrodynamic instabilities from isolated internal defects limit performance in inertial confinement fusion experiments; the authors aim to extend dynamic stabilization via modulated laser pulses to mitigate these instabilities.
method: The authors extend the concept of dynamic stabilization using temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive to the prepulse regime, analyzing the effect on isolated internal defects through theoretical modeling and simulations.
result: The temporally modulated laser prepulse dynamically stabilizes the isolated internal defect, reducing instability growth.
conclusion: Dynamic stabilization via modulated laser prepulses is a promising technique to improve inertial confinement fusion performance by mitigating defect-seeded instabilities.

title: Self-propelled Droplet Dynamics On Superhydrophobic Surfaces Under Low-pressure Conditions
authors: Xiaonan Li, Jiayi Zhou, Haiyan Luo, Xueli Zheng, And Guo Chen

The self-removal of sessile droplets under low-pressure conditions is critical for extreme-environment surface engineering. Combining high-speed photography with quantitative analysis, we reveal the unique dynamics of ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhyd…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065506] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of self-propelled droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces under low pressure, focusing on fluid mechanics and surface engineering.
motivation: Understanding droplet self-removal under low pressure is important for extreme-environment surface engineering applications.
method: High-speed photography and quantitative analysis are used to observe ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhydrophobic surfaces.
result: The study reveals unique droplet dynamics under low-pressure conditions, including self-propulsion and removal mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing surfaces that can self-clean or remove droplets in low-pressure environments.

title: Plume Stretching In The Trapped Region Of A Reoriented Potential Mixer
authors: Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, And Tomás G. Dabove

The reoriented potential mixer (RPM) can enhance mixing and reaction during in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater, in which a chemical or biological amendment is introduced into a contaminant plume to react with and degrade the contaminant. Each step of the RPM consists of dipole flow betw…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065108] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid mixing in a reoriented potential mixer for groundwater remediation, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Enhance in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater by improving mixing and reaction between introduced amendments and contaminant plumes.
method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow and numerical simulations.
result: Quantifies stretching dynamics and mixing efficiency in the trapped region under reoriented potential mixing.
conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing in trapped regions, aiding remediation efforts.

title: Equivalency Of Spike-frequency And H-current-based Adaptation In A Wilson-Cowan Field Model
authors: Ronja Strömsdörfer And Klaus Obermayer
abstract:
Author(s): Ronja Strömsdörfer and Klaus Obermayer

During slow-wave sleep, the brain produces traveling waves of slow oscillations (SOs; [MATH]), characterized by the propagation of alternating high- and low-activity states. They play a crucial role in memory consolidation and are frequently investigated, empirical…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023348] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spike-frequency adaptation and H-current-based adaptation in a Wilson-Cowan field model of slow-wave sleep, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms of traveling waves during slow-wave sleep, which are important for memory consolidation.
method: The authors develop a Wilson-Cowan field model incorporating spike-frequency adaptation and H-current-based adaptation, and analyze the resulting wave dynamics.
result: They show that the two adaptation mechanisms can produce equivalent wave patterns under certain conditions.
conclusion: The equivalence suggests that different biological mechanisms may underlie the same observed phenomena, aiding in model selection and interpretation.

title: Redirecting Countermoving Swarms Through Collision
authors: Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy Mcguire, And Ira B. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy McGuire, and Ira B. Schwartz

Multiswarm systems, where two or more swarms of mobile agents occupy the same region of space with different parameters and goals, occur in a variety of biological, engineering, and defense applications. Composites of multiple swarms can produce hybrid spatiotemporal patterns, which compared to sing…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023351] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of multiple swarms of mobile agents that collide and redirect each other, focusing on pattern formation and control.
motivation: Understanding how multiple swarms with different goals interact in the same space is important for biological, engineering, and defense applications.
method: The authors model multiswarm systems using agent-based simulations and analyze the resulting spatiotemporal patterns, particularly the effect of collisions on swarm redirection.
result: They find that collisions can lead to hybrid patterns and enable redirection of countermoving swarms, with potential for control strategies.
conclusion: Collision-mediated interactions in multiswarm systems can be harnessed for redirecting swarms, offering insights for collective behavior and robotic swarms.

title: Parametric Resonance, Chaos, And Spatial Structure In The Lotka-Volterra Model
authors: Mohamed Swailem And Alastair M. Rucklidge
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamed Swailem and Alastair M. Rucklidge

We investigate the Lotka-Volterra model for predator-prey competition with a finite carrying capacity that varies periodically in time, modeling seasonal variations in nutrients or food resources. In the absence of time variability, the ordinary differential equations have an equilibrium point that …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023352] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parametric resonance and chaos in the Lotka-Volterra predator-prey model with periodic carrying capacity.
motivation: Understanding how seasonal variations affect predator-prey dynamics and spatial pattern formation.
method: Numerical simulations and bifurcation analysis of the Lotka-Volterra equations with time-periodic carrying capacity.
result: Identified parametric resonance and chaotic behavior, and characterized spatial structures in the model.
conclusion: Seasonal forcing can induce complex dynamics including chaos and spatial patterns in ecological systems.

title: Dispersed-phase Forcing Reorganizes Lagrangian Intermittency In Turbulence
authors: Zecai Zhou, Hendrik Hessenkemper, Andrew D. Bragg, And Tian Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Zecai Zhou, Hendrik Hessenkemper, Andrew D. Bragg, and Tian Ma

In single-phase turbulence, fluctuations in the Lagrangian velocity increments become more extreme as the timescale [MATH] decreases, leading to the strongest fluctuations as [MATH]. Using high-resolution three-dimensional Lagrangian particle tracking experiments, we find that for turbulent flows where …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023338] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Lagrangian intermittency in turbulent flows with dispersed particles, focusing on fluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how dispersed-phase forcing modifies extreme fluctuations in Lagrangian velocity increments in turbulence.
method: High-resolution 3D Lagrangian particle tracking experiments in turbulent flows with dispersed particles.
result: Dispersed-phase forcing reorganizes Lagrangian intermittency, altering the statistics of extreme velocity increments.
conclusion: The presence of dispersed particles significantly changes the intermittent behavior of turbulence, with implications for multiphase flow modeling.

title: Estimating Orbital Parameters Of Direct Imaging Exoplanet Using Neural Networks
authors: Bo Liang, Chang Liu, Hanlin Song, Tianyu Zhao, Yuxiang Xu, Zihao Xiao, Manjia Liang, Minghui Du, Wei-Liang Qian, Li-E Qiang, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, And Ziren Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Liang, Chang Liu, Hanlin Song, Tianyu Zhao, Yuxiang Xu, Zihao Xiao, Manjia Liang, Minghui Du, Wei-Liang Qian, Li-e Qiang, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, and Ziren Luo

We propose a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo (FM-MCMC) algorithm for estimating the orbital parameters of exoplanetary systems, especially for those in which only one exoplanet is involved. Compared to traditional methods that rely on random sampling within the Bayesian framework, our approac…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023341] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to estimate orbital parameters of directly imaged exoplanets.
motivation: Traditional Bayesian methods for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation rely on random sampling, which can be inefficient. The authors aim to improve efficiency and accuracy using a flow-matching approach.
method: The authors propose a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo (FM-MCMC) algorithm that combines normalizing flows with MCMC to sample from the posterior distribution of orbital parameters.
result: The FM-MCMC algorithm demonstrates improved convergence and accuracy compared to standard MCMC methods on simulated and real exoplanet data.
conclusion: Flow-matching MCMC is a promising tool for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation, offering better performance than traditional sampling methods.

title: Enhanced Plasma Production By Ambipolar Electric Fields In Convergent Magnetic Fields
authors: Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, And Antonella Caldarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, and Antonella Caldarelli

Controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency (rf) plasma source is demonstrated by placing magnetic nozzle throat several tens of centimeters away from the rf antenna, where a local density peak forms near the throat. The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma production in a convergent magnetic field using ambipolar electric fields, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve controlled unidirectional remote plasma production for applications in plasma propulsion or processing.
method: Experimental demonstration using a radio-frequency plasma source with a magnetic nozzle throat placed away from the antenna, measuring density and electron energy.
result: A local density peak forms near the throat, indicating dominant electron energization by ambipolar electric fields in the convergent magnetic field.
conclusion: Ambipolar electric fields in convergent magnetic fields can enhance plasma production, enabling remote plasma generation.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022055] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a proof-of-principle experiment on beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To demonstrate a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators, combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal.
method: The experiment used stable resonance islands and a bent crystal to split and channel a circulating proton beam onto an absorber, emulating slow extraction over millions of turns.
result: Successful proof-of-principle: the beam was extracted with low loss, validating the theoretical proposal.
conclusion: This technique offers a promising option for future accelerator extraction systems, potentially reducing losses and eliminating the need for a septum.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts applications like flow stabilization. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications by maintaining an out-of-phase response over a wide frequency range.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]

motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K; this erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely involves corrections to experimental data or analysis from the original study.
result: The erratum reports corrections to the published results.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated, resembling the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: Derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new path for materials design by linking geometry and mechanics.
conclusion: The approach offers a different perspective for engineering metamaterials with tailored mechanical responses.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and develop a force-response model to connect single-molecule behavior to bulk fatigue properties.
result: They identify key molecular determinants of fatigue and demonstrate how protein unfolding and refolding cycles govern crack propagation in hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a design strategy for fatigue-resistant hydrogels by engineering protein-based crosslinks with controlled mechanical stability.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work links microscopic ion motion to macroscopic properties, aiding material design.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects drive cell extrusion in curved tissues is important for developmental biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate epithelial sheets with curvature and analyze cell shapes and forces.
result: They find that cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate bulging and extrusion, with curvature modulating these effects.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the mechanobiology of epithelial tissues, linking geometry to cell fate.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding microhydrodynamics of swimming microorganisms is important for biology and physics, but the paper focuses on fluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming alga.
result: Discovery of unexpected flow structures at low Reynolds numbers.
conclusion: The findings expand understanding of microhydrodynamics and have biological implications for microbial motility.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: To understand strong interaction (QCD) through charmonium decays and search for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on e+e- collisions producing open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Hadron production in charm-meson pairs provides key insights into QCD, and BESIII data will continue to advance the field.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its legacy in planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the Arecibo Observatory's contributions and highlight its impact on various scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial compilation of colloquia, not a research study with a specific method.
result: The editorial presents a historical overview of Arecibo's achievements.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a revolutionary impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To document the contributions of the Arecibo planetary radar system to planetary science and its role in supporting in situ exploration.
method: The paper presents a historical overview of radar techniques and summarizes key observations of planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.
result: Arecibo radar provided unique subsurface and surface data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary radar astronomy, and its loss leaves a significant gap.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Arecibo made major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled groundbreaking discoveries across astronomy and atmospheric science.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments, focusing on ionospheric and atmospheric physics.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research, highlighting the capabilities of its incoherent scatter radar.
method: Review of experimental techniques including incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and optical sensors, and their application to study plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The paper presents advances in understanding ionospheric dynamics, metal layers, and coupling processes, enabled by Arecibo's unique instrumentation.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing analysis and future directions.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The paper synthesizes experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud microphysics.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate controlled turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising platform to address the long-standing bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos would greatly enhance understanding.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest predictions for gravitational wave signatures from neutrino-driven core collapse supernovae and outlines multimessenger observation strategies.
conclusion: A Galactic supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and current detectors are poised to capture gravitational waves from such an event.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, challenging the cosmological principle.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole in galaxy/quasar catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including checks for biases and systematics.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model and motivate further investigation into alternative cosmological models.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a survey of remaining viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels for various supersymmetric scenarios at the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of the status of supersymmetry and outlines the expected sensitivity of the HL-LHC to different models.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but highly constrained; the HL-LHC will probe significant remaining parameter space.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work from the last decade on nuclear reactions, plasma and atomic physics in the solar environment.
result: It summarizes advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma effects, and diagnostics like solar neutrinos and helioseismology.
conclusion: The review provides an updated model of the solar interior based on recent data and theory.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022

abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.

motivation: To provide a self-consistent set of fundamental constants for use in physics and chemistry.
method: Least-squares adjustment of all available data up to the end of 2022.
result: Updated values for constants such as Planck constant, speed of light, etc.
conclusion: The new recommended values supersede previous CODATA sets and are the standard reference.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, focusing on turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Gas bubble dynamics are important in many natural and industrial processes, but the field lacks a comprehensive review of recent advances.
method: The authors survey experimental, theoretical, and numerical studies over the past 20 years, organizing findings by key factors such as turbulence, rheology, and surfactants.
result: Key advances include improved understanding of bubble deformation, added mass effects, and interactions with turbulent flows and non-Newtonian fluids.
conclusion: The review provides a framework for modeling bubble dynamics and identifies open questions for future research.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on polar active particles that align their orientation with their velocity.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment, as opposed to neighbor imitation, leads to novel collective behaviors in active matter.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments, and proposes a unified mathematical framework for self-alignment in active systems.
result: Self-alignment enables phenomena such as orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, with applications in biology and robotics.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that can be harnessed for designing smart materials and robotic swarms.

abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory.
